[Subscribe](https://substack.com/redirect/985822be-86af-465e-b45d-8338a50f508c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
Here's the thing that makes me want to pull my hair out. As frustrating as Fetterman is, and he is, he still votes with us 85-90% percent of the time depending on the day. His views on abortion, on gay rights, on a whole list of issues are basically in line with mine. Yes, he's gone off the reservation on Israel and a few other things in ways that make no sense to me. But in how he talks and how he votes, he is still a Democrat.
What's killing him at home is how he spends his time. He doesn't introduce legislation. He doesn't do constituent services. He has never given a single speech on the floor of the United States Senate. He spends his energy on cable news parroting Republican talking points instead of doing the job. That's why he's so unpopular in his own state.
And Republicans have flocked to this guy anyway. Not because he votes with them. He literally votes against them. They love him for exactly one reason: he pisses off people like you and me. That's it. That's the whole appeal.
**They prefer a Democrat who makes liberals mad on the internet to a Republican who actually delivers for them on the floor. Think about how empty you have to be for that to be your standard.**
Because that's the defining characteristic of the modern MAGA movement. It doesn't believe in anything except annoying its opposition. It's what drove Trump's reelection in 2024. It's what drives the army of MAGA influencers being paid unbelievable sums by Trump's super PAC and by foreign governments pumping money into this thing.
None of them have a meaningful solution for anything. Not for ending this war, not for fixing the economy, not for rooting out the corruption in our government, not for building a single program that would make your life or your family's life stronger. Which is what government is supposed to be about. It's that Paul Wellstone quote I bring up all the time: politics is about the improvement of people's lives. We are so far from that right now it makes me sick.
The Republican Party today is not a party of ideas. It's a party built entirely out of grievance. They're still mad Barack Obama got elected in 2008, so it's fine if Trump steals billions of dollars, because we didn't like Trump the way they didn't like Obama. It's fine for Trump to use the power of the federal government to go after his political enemies because Roseanne Barr got fired from ABC. You hear this shit constantly.
There's a grievance and a rationalization for everything, and it has rotted them to the point where they see Fetterman trashing Democrats on Hannity over a couple of issues and say, he's our guy, we love him.
* * *
_Framing can completely change a story when you 're only seeing one version of it. Ground News brings together coverage from 50,000+ sources, giving you different perspectives so you can see the full picture and decide for yourself what you think._
_My team and I use it because it helps cut through the noise._
**[See every side of every story with Ground News->](https://substack.com/redirect/985822be-86af-465e-b45d-8338a50f508c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[Subscribe](https://substack.com/redirect/985822be-86af-465e-b45d-8338a50f508c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
And here's the part Fetterman himself doesn't seem to understand. Washington Republicans are playing the same clever game they always play. They're making him feel powerful and special and important. They're lining up the next act for him, the Fox News contributor gig, exactly what they did for Joe Manchin, who is on TV every single day trashing Democrats and, I'm sure, being paid handsomely for it by somebody.
But when Fetterman's not in the room, they mock him. I've got a clip I'm playing on YouTube later today of them making fun of how he was dressed just a few days ago.
That's the deal. Flatter him to his face so he stays a useful idiot against Democrats through the midterms, laugh at him behind his back, and the minute he stops being useful, pull his airtime and send him back to being as irrelevant as he was before he got to the Senate.
What makes it maddening is that most of what Fetterman now complains about in the Democratic Party is exactly what got him elected. He ran as a progressive insurgent. If he'd run as a moderate and governed as a moderate, fine, that's what Manchin did in West Virginia, and I didn't love it, but Manchin was probably the best we were ever going to get out of West Virginia.
Fetterman is nowhere close to the best we can get out of Pennsylvania. We can do so much better, and I cannot wait for the inevitable primary. He can't win a Democratic primary. His only path is as an independent or maybe as a Republican, and I'm not convinced he wins that either, McCormick numbers or not.
Zoom out and this is the whole picture of Washington right now. A petty game. So many of the people we spend all day arguing about and pleading with to move legislation that might actually improve your life are just pieces on a board, moved around by a handful of entities hoping you don't notice the real story.
Your life is getting worse every single day, and Donald Trump's life is getting better every single day, because he's stuffing money into his own pockets and the pockets of his family and people like Jared Kushner and the billionaire buddies who are all over the Epstein files.
I don't enjoy spending this much time on a member of my own party. I track the Fetterman story this closely because he represents something deeply broken in our politics.
And I don't believe him when he says he won't switch. I think he waits for the moment it hurts the most. Democrats win 51 seats, he hands the Senate back to Trump, and Trump shoves another Supreme Court justice down our throats. It's disgusting. We can't look away from this just because he's got a D next to his name. Something is wrong here, and it's a symptom of the whole damn broken system.
With urgency,
--Mike

His only path is as an independent or maybe as a Republican, and I'm not convinced he wins that either, McCormick numbers or not. Zoom out and this is the whole picture of Washington right now. A petty game. So many of the people we spend all day arguing about and pleading with to move legislation that might actually improve your life are just pieces on a board, moved around by a handful of entities hoping you don't notice the real story. Your life is getting worse every single day, and Donald Trump's life is getting better every single day, because he's stuffing money into his own pockets and the pockets of his family and people like Jared Kushner and the billionaire buddies who are all over the Epstein files. I don't enjoy spending this much time on a member of my own party. I track the Fetterman story this closely because he represents something deeply broken in our politics. And I don't believe him when he says he won't switch. I think he waits for the moment it hurts the most. Democrats win 51 seats, he hands the Senate back to Trump, and Trump shoves another Supreme Court justice down our throats. It's disgusting. We can't look away from this just because he's got a D next to his name. Something is wrong here, and it's a symptom of the whole damn broken system. In just 69 days, we have the opportunity to change course: to flip the House and build a firewall against Trump’s dangerous agenda, one climate champion at a time, in city councils, statehouses, Congress, and beyond, brick by brick, until there’s nowhere left for Big Oil to hide. = If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | = | = ---|--- = | = = | = Your donation could be the difference between getting close and sending a true climate champion into the halls of power. ### **American Strength Must Be Built in America**
---
| | | | [ ](https://7bnf5.r.a.d.sendibm1.com/mk/cl/f/sh/7nVU1aA2nfuMSVdkFHJd28ECivtlfBE/thstjpc79glV)
---
| | | | A nation’s strength cannot be judged just by the magnitude of its economy, the level of its stock market, or the extent of its banking institutions. True national strength lies in a people’s ability to produce the goods needed to maintain their way of life.
The United States needs to have the ability to manufacture medicine for its hospitals, transformers for its electrical grid, semiconductors for its technology, machinery for its factories, vehicles for its economy, and weapons for its defense. It isn’t just losing jobs when a country loses these capabilities; it is, in effect, giving up a certain degree of its independence.
Manufacturing forms the basis of the visible economy. Since most people do not take much time to think about foundations because they are generally out of sight, everyone in the structure eventually feels the effects when the foundation starts to deteriorate.
Over more than four decades, America has allowed that foundation to erode.
The Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that American manufacturing employment had reached a record high of 19.6 million jobs in June 1979, while by [July 2026](https://7bnf5.r.a.d.sendibm1.com/mk/cl/f/sh/7nVU1aA2nfwFS293DqY54UY0tIOYP7k/_IyXUUciyd5Q) it had dropped to about 12.6 million. Although the American population increased significantly over that time, the country had nearly seven million fewer manufacturing workers. This represents a decline of roughly 36% from the 1979 peak.
---
| | | | [ READ MORE](https://7bnf5.r.a.d.sendibm1.com/mk/cl/f/sh/7nVU1aA2nfy8RYeMCPmX6qrp3etL94G/46rbpFbUjNsg)

# **Iowa State Fair 2026**
---
| | | | |
---
|
---
| |
---
|
---
|
---
| | | My recent trip to Iowa reminded me where the true strength of America resides. It is not found in Washington, D.C. It lives in the men and women who rise each morning, work hard, raise their families, serve their communities, worship God, and still believe this country is worth fighting for.
Across Iowa, I had the privilege of meeting farmers, veterans, law enforcement officers, small business owners, parents, and young Americans who are hungry for honest leadership and a renewed sense of national purpose. They are not asking the government to solve every problem. They want safe communities, economic opportunity, accountable government, and the freedom to build a better life for their children.
The photographs capture only a few moments from my time in Iowa, but they reflect something much larger. The spirit of America is still alive. Our people remain strong, determined, and ready to fight for the country they love.

New poll shows Democratic voters overwhelmingly think Israel is committing genocide in Gaza. 47 killed in Haiti in gang raid near capital. U.S. removes Syria from terrorism list. * * *
# Palestine
* **Killed and wounded in Gaza:** Over the past 24 hours, nine Palestinians were killed--six in new Israeli attacks and two due to wounds sustained in earlier attacks--and 36 were injured in attacks across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. One body was recovered from beneath the rubble.
* The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 has risen to 73,431 killed, with 174,437 injured. Since October 11, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,296 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 4,296, while 814 bodies have been recovered from under the rubble.
* **Israel continues to strike Gaza despite "ceasefire": **Israeli strikes on Gaza [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/927a6dbc-08e2-40dc-b584-7d5632099ff4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) nine Palestinians, including two children, on Monday, with attacks reported on homes, tents, prayer halls, and a desalination plant.
* Israeli forces struck a home east of Bureij refugee camp, killing a four-year-old child and trapping residents under rubble.
* Israeli aircraft bombed the Ashkelon prayer hall and a home in Al-Shati camp, wounding residents.
* An overnight drone strike on a tent near Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital killed two brothers.
* Israeli forces killed two more Palestinians in strikes on Khan Younis, with one Palestinian dying on Tuesday from wounds sustained in the strikes.
* **Israel shoots 10-year-old Palestinian girl in the back, killing her in Gaza tent:** Israeli forces shot 10-year-old girl Amal Abu Khater in the back, killing her instantly as she sat eating lunch inside her displaced family's tent in western Khan Younis, southern Gaza, on Monday. Amal had just returned from memorizing the Quran and performing the Dhuhr prayer, her family told Drop Site's Mohamed Ahmed.
* "There were people who felt safe, sitting in their tents. It's supposed to be a safe area, and it is full of displaced people," Amal's relative Hassan Abu Khater told Drop Site.
* "What did she do to deserve to be killed? She was sitting and eating sweets... What sin did this little girl commit?" Amal's grandmother, Samira Abu Khater, said.
* **Watch Ahmed 's dispatch from Khan Younis [here](https://substack.com/redirect/cdbed250-8bda-424a-9b6c-f47a1abb76c2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).**
* **Israeli forces seize UNRWA center in East Jerusalem, expel staff:** Israeli forces [raided](https://substack.com/redirect/7f59a9b8-2be8-4ad2-b9dc-8742a328d87e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and seized the UNRWA-run Qalandiya Vocational Training Centre in Kafr Aqab, north of occupied East Jerusalem on Tuesday, storming the compound with four armored vehicles and 50 Israeli security forces and raising an Israeli flag inside. Around 40 employees and others inside were detained and questioned before being expelled, with Israeli forces firing tear gas around the center. Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir participated in the raid.
* The seized UNRWA compound would be replaced with an educational and community center, the Israeli Foreign Ministry said, while claiming the land has been owned by the Jewish National Fund since 1937. The facility, established in 1952 and which had hosted a diplomatic mission on Monday investigating Israeli attacks, is UNRWA's oldest vocational training center and trains roughly 340 young Palestinian refugees annually.
* The seizure marked a shift "from raids and restrictions to eviction and imposing control on a United Nations facility," the Jerusalem Governorate [said](https://substack.com/redirect/864501cd-0a88-4750-97fe-7e52e6ffa3b8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in a statement. It warned that the move was part of "an Israeli plan targeting the Palestinian presence and international institutions in Jerusalem."
* **Settler attacks and Israeli raids in the occupied West Bank** :
* **Bethlehem** : Israeli settlers [attacked](https://substack.com/redirect/272a4d48-8a9d-4426-9c3f-d7cfded34609?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) international solidarity activists near Harmala on Tuesday morning, choking and bruising several during the assault. The activists were attempting to open a road that had been closed by the settlers; the settlers assaulted them with sticks and pepper spray. Settlers [injured](https://substack.com/redirect/86e2f7d6-70b1-4865-bd9d-175c2bfe7678?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) three Palestinians Tuesday in the Al-Hashwa area east of Bethlehem, WAFA reported. Separately, Israeli forces detained three Palestinians in the governorate, including Palestinian journalist Thaer Al-Fakhouri.
* **Ramallah:** Settlers [prevented](https://substack.com/redirect/151976ea-53f7-416b-9049-a7fc88947c96?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) firefighting crews from reaching a fire that broke out on agricultural land in Wadi Ammar, northeast of Ramallah, delaying efforts to extinguish the blaze.
* **Nablus:** Settlers have continued to besiege three Palestinian homes in Qusra, south of Nablus, for a third consecutive week. Israeli forces have also tightened restrictions and closed roads leading to the area.
* **Jenin:** Israeli forces [uprooted](https://substack.com/redirect/5b34ad73-a304-41a0-8ecd-2378c746945c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) more than 100 olive trees in Wadi Al-Yahmour in Barta'a, southwest of Jenin.
* **Jordan Valley:** Israeli forces [arrested](https://substack.com/redirect/61b0b87e-3a83-4597-8cd7-be0bd5f1f968?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a 16-year-old Palestinian after he reportedly ambushed and stabbed an Israeli soldier outside a commercial complex. The soldier sustained wounds, including internal bleeding, and is hospitalized in stable condition.
* **Iconic Palestinian artist Sliman Mansour passes at 79:** Palestinian artist Sliman Mansour, whose work became a visual language of Palestinian identity, land, and resistance, has died at the age of 79, his family announced Monday. "The final chapter has been written," his family said. "To the world, he leaves behind a life filled with beauty, memory, and a legacy that will continue to live through all those he touched."
* Born in Birzeit in 1947, a year prior to the Nakba and the expulsion of more than 700,000 Palestinians by Israeli militias, Mansour spent more than five decades depicting a Palestine rooted in its people and landscape.

Palestinian artists and activists drew inspiration from Mansour's story and started using the watermelon as a symbol of their identity. During the First Intifada, he co-founded the New Visions collective, with artists boycotting Israeli art supplies and instead working with mud and henna, incorporating Palestine into their art.

This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Palestine Killed and wounded in Gaza: Over the past 24 hours, nine Palestinians were killed--six in new Israeli attacks and two due to wounds sustained in earlier attacks--and 36 were injured in attacks across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. One body was recovered from beneath the rubble. The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 has risen to 73,431 killed, with 174,437 injured. Since October 11, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,296 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 4,296, while 814 bodies have been recovered from under the rubble. Israel continues to strike Gaza despite "ceasefire": Israeli strikes on Gaza nine Palestinians, including two children, on Monday, with attacks reported on homes, tents, prayer halls, and a desalination plant. Israeli forces struck a home east of Bureij refugee camp, killing a four-year-old child and trapping residents under rubble. Israeli aircraft bombed the Ashkelon prayer hall and a home in Al-Shati camp, wounding residents. An overnight drone strike on a tent near Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital killed two brothers. Israeli forces killed two more Palestinians in strikes on Khan Younis, with one Palestinian dying on Tuesday from wounds sustained in the strikes. Israel shoots 10-year-old Palestinian girl in the back, killing her in Gaza tent: Israeli forces shot 10-year-old girl Amal Abu Khater in the back, killing her instantly as she sat eating lunch inside her displaced family's tent in western Khan Younis, southern Gaza, on Monday. Amal had just returned from memorizing the Quran and performing the Dhuhr prayer, her family told Drop Site's Mohamed Ahmed. "There were people who felt safe, sitting in their tents. It's supposed to be a safe area, and it is full of displaced people," Amal's relative Hassan Abu Khater told Drop Site. "What did she do to deserve to be killed? She was sitting and eating sweets... What sin did this little girl commit?" Amal's grandmother, Samira Abu Khater, said. Watch Ahmed 's dispatch from Khan Younis . Israeli forces seize UNRWA center in East Jerusalem, expel staff: Israeli forces and seized the UNRWA-run Qalandiya Vocational Training Centre in Kafr Aqab, north of occupied East Jerusalem on Tuesday, storming the compound with four armored vehicles and 50 Israeli security forces and raising an Israeli flag inside. Around 40 employees and others inside were detained and questioned before being expelled, with Israeli forces firing tear gas around the center. Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir participated in the raid. The seized UNRWA compound would be replaced with an educational and community center, the Israeli Foreign Ministry said, while claiming the land has been owned by the Jewish National Fund since 1937. The facility, established in 1952 and which had hosted a diplomatic mission on Monday investigating Israeli attacks, is UNRWA's oldest vocational training center and trains roughly 340 young Palestinian refugees annually. The seizure marked a shift "from raids and restrictions to eviction and imposing control on a United Nations facility," the Jerusalem Governorate in a statement. It warned that the move was part of "an Israeli plan targeting the Palestinian presence and international institutions in Jerusalem." Settler attacks and Israeli raids in the occupied West Bank : Bethlehem : Israeli settlers international solidarity activists near Harmala on Tuesday morning, choking and bruising several during the assault. The activists were attempting to open a road that had been closed by the settlers; the settlers assaulted them with sticks and pepper spray. Settlers three Palestinians Tuesday in the Al-Hashwa area east of Bethlehem, WAFA reported. Separately, Israeli forces detained three Palestinians in the governorate, including Palestinian journalist Thaer Al-Fakhouri. Ramallah: Settlers firefighting crews from reaching a fire that broke out on agricultural land in Wadi Ammar, northeast of Ramallah, delaying efforts to extinguish the blaze. Nablus: Settlers have continued to besiege three Palestinian homes in Qusra, south of Nablus, for a third consecutive week. Israeli forces have also tightened restrictions and closed roads leading to the area. Jenin: Israeli forces more than 100 olive trees in Wadi Al-Yahmour in Barta'a, southwest of Jenin. Jordan Valley: Israeli forces a 16-year-old Palestinian after he reportedly ambushed and stabbed an Israeli soldier outside a commercial complex. The soldier sustained wounds, including internal bleeding, and is hospitalized in stable condition. Iconic Palestinian artist Sliman Mansour passes at 79: Palestinian artist Sliman Mansour, whose work became a visual language of Palestinian identity, land, and resistance, has died at the age of 79, his family announced Monday. "The final chapter has been written," his family said. "To the world, he leaves behind a life filled with beauty, memory, and a legacy that will continue to live through all those he touched." Born in Birzeit in 1947, a year prior to the Nakba and the expulsion of more than 700,000 Palestinians by Israeli militias, Mansour spent more than five decades depicting a Palestine rooted in its people and landscape. His work was repeatedly targeted by Israeli authorities. In 1980, the Israeli military shut down an exhibition featuring Mansour in Ramallah just three hours after it opened. Mansour later recalled that the artists were summoned and told they could not use the colors of the Palestinian flag, even in depictions of flowers or watermelons. Palestinian artists and activists drew inspiration from Mansour's story and started using the watermelon as a symbol of their identity. During the First Intifada, he co-founded the New Visions collective, with artists boycotting Israeli art supplies and instead working with mud and henna, incorporating Palestine into their art. | ---|--- Sliman Mansour on Instagram: "Camel of Hardship, also known as... Iran Oil tanker struck off Omani coast: An oil tanker was by an "unknown projectile" off northern Oman on Monday, damaging its engine room and disabling the vessel, according to the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO). The attack occurred 9 nautical miles northeast of Ash Shishah, on Oman's Musandam Peninsula near the entrance to the Strait of Hormuz. UKMTO said the crew was safe, but the environmental impact remained unknown. No group claimed responsibility. U.S. unveils latest wave of Iran sanctions: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent sanctions against nearly 60 people, entities, and vessels on Monday, dubbing the campaign "Operation Economic Outcast," aimed at disrupting Iran's global financial and economic connections. The announcement provided few details regarding secondary sanctions on countries that do business with Iran, and Bessent declined to identify the countries that would be targeted or say when penalties would take effect. China, Turkey, and the United Arab Emirates are Iran's largest trade partners. Bessent claimed that U.S. President Donald Trump is now personally calling world leaders and asking them to end dealings with Tehran. Seyed Ali Madanizadeh, Iran's Economy Minister, to Monday's announcement by curtly noting that the U.S. would "fail this time as well" to hinder Iran, and adding that the country had "long been preparing for days like this." Iranian Parliament Speaker and lead negotiator Mohammed Bagher Ghalibaf also a statement, writing on X that Iran's trading partners had made clear to Tehran that they would completely disregard Washington's threats. "They don't take these statements into account at all," Ghalibaf said. Qatari Foreign Ministry spokesperson Majed Al-Ansari described the U.S. sanctions on Iran as unilateral, instead reaffirming Doha's support for mediation between Washington and Tehran. China warns U.S. sanctions on Iran 's trade partners will "only intensify tensions": China it would take "necessary measures to safeguard its legitimate rights and interests." Ahead of Bessent's announcement, the Foreign Ministry warned that "sanctions and pressure do not help solve problems; they only intensify tensions." NYT: U.S. prepares to return diplomats to Middle East embassies evacuated during Iran war: The U.S. is to return diplomats to several Middle Eastern embassies evacuated during the war with Iran, the New York Times reported. Foreign Service officers could begin returning as early as this week to missions in Israel, Lebanon, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Jordan, Oman, Iraq, and Kuwait, according to an internal State Department document obtained by the Times. The U.S. Embassy in Lebanon is expected to receive returning diplomats first but will remain below full staffing, while missions in Israel, Jordan, and Oman are eventually expected to return in full. IEA not discussing second emergency oil release: International Energy Agency chief Fatih Birol Reuters on Monday that the agency is not currently considering a second release from member countries' strategic oil reserves. "Not for the time being," he said, adding that 80% of the reserves remain after member nations announced a 400 million-barrel release in March. Birol also warned that Europe could face gas shortages during the winter. European storage is around 62%, below historical averages and short of the EU's target of 80% by December 1, as the bloc seeks to eliminate Russian imports while still hoping to receive supplies from the Middle East. Tehran hosts Pakistan Army Chief: Pakistani army chief Field Marshal Asim Munir and Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi in Tehran on Monday. Naqvi said that Munir's meeting with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian made "significant progress" toward restoring the Islamabad memorandum between Iran and the United States. The Interior Minister said Pezeshkian presented Tehran's concerns and the meeting ended on a "highly positive note." Maj. Gen. Mohsen Rezaei, the Secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, reportedly his Pakistani counterparts that Iran "distrusts the United States," and that it must "change its behavior" before any talks, urging the U.S. to "implement the terms" of the previous memorandum of understanding. Omani Foreign Minister visits Iran for talks on Hormuz: Oman's Foreign Minister Sayyid Badr Albusaidi in Tehran on Tuesday for talks about the Strait of Hormuz. Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei described the conversations as strictly bilateral, having nothing to do with the U.S. Shipping data showed just two tankers crossed the Strait on Monday, down from seven vessels on Sunday. Trump claimed Tuesday that the U.S. Navy had removed or detonated all mines in international waters in the Strait, saying in a on Truth Social that Iran had been warned that any vessel laying new mines would be "immediately and systematically destroyed." Iran 's central bank chief calls currency collapse "temporary" as rial hits record low: Iran's currency to a record low of about 2.02 million rials to the U.S. dollar on Monday. Central Bank governor Abdolnaser Hemmati insisted the depreciation was "temporary, meaning they fluctuate," in remarks aired on state TV, and reported by The New Arab. The rial has lost nearly 10% in two weeks, on top of a plunge early in the war. Yemen Saudi confirms Ansarallah attack on tanker: Saudi national shipping company Bahri Monday that its tanker Amzan had been attacked in the Red Sea. Ansarallah said it struck the vessel with a ballistic missile off Yanbu, causing a fire. Bahri said the crew was safe and reported no injuries. Yanbu has become Saudi Arabia's main oil export route since Iran blockaded the Strait of Hormuz. Lebanon Israel continues violating ceasefire across southern Lebanon, bombing Tyre and advancing in Bint Jbeil: In the Tyre district, Israeli aircraft two strikes on Mansouri and another on Wadi Hassan on Tuesday, alongside extensive demolition operations in Mansouri and Majdal Zoun, Lebanon's National News Agency reported. Israeli forces fired toward Ainata and Beit Lif in the Bint Jbeil district, while military vehicles advanced from Hadatha. In Marjayoun, Israeli artillery shelling near the Hamames hill a fire, while Israeli forces new earth barriers near Kfar Kila and Tall Al-Nahhas, including one roughly 150 meters from inhabited homes in Burj Al-Muluk. On Monday evening, a major explosion was in Zawtar Sharqieh, in Nabatieh district, while an Israeli drone dropped a stun grenade near rescue crews in Dohat Kfar Roummane. No injuries were reported. Additional shelling hit Yater, Braasheet and Ainata, while two new airstrikes hit Mansouri. Israeli forces also carried out demolitions and detonations in Houla. U.S. News U.S. kills two in eastern Pacific boat strike: The U.S. military conducted a strike on a boat in the eastern Pacific on Monday, killing two people, according to U.S. Southern Command. SOUTHCOM posted of the strike and said it "executed a lethal kinetic strike on a low-profile vessel," claiming without evidence it was engaged in narco-trafficking. The Trump administration's targeting of vessels has killed at least 223 people in dozens of strikes on boats in the Pacific and Caribbean since September 2025. Senate runoff in South Carolina: Darline Graham , the sister of the late Sen. Lindsey Graham Rep. Ralph Norman in today's South Carolina Republican senatorial runoff. Graham received more than $827,000 worth of calls and text messages in the runup to the primary from Trump's MAGA Inc. super PAC, the first significant expenditure for the PAC, which has $400 million in reserve. U.S.-Canada trade dispute escalates: President Donald Trump Canada on Monday to "fall in line" or face tariffs "far WORSE" than existing ones and threatened new 50% tariffs on Canadian vehicles, auto parts, and steel starting next year. Prime Minister Mark Carney , whose government is expected to announce retaliatory tariffs on Tuesday, accused Washington of trying to "destroy [its] major industries" and treat Canada as "a subsidiary of the United States." Trump also attacked Ontario Premier Doug Ford as "the less charismatic, intelligent, and overall unimpressive brother of the late, great Rob Ford" after Ford said Canadians were prepared for "an economic war" and threatened to cut off electricity and critical minerals if the dispute worsens. Treasury could tap $1 trillion cash account to fund bond buybacks, officials say: The Treasury Department use its nearly $1 trillion general account to help fund an announced increase in long-term government bond purchases, according to two senior Treasury officials cited by CNBC. The move follows Secretary Scott Bessent 's surprise announcement that Treasury would double buybacks of off-the-run securities from $2 billion to at least $4 billion. The bond market, which was skeptical of Bessent's ability to do this, saw its yields sharply rise. The TGA, essentially the government's cash reserve held at the Federal Reserve, currently has around $950 billion, well above the roughly $550-600 billion target set under the Biden administration, and officials said tapping it--rather than relying solely on short-term bill sales, as Bessent's "Treasury Twist" comment suggested--would give the operation more firepower while avoiding any need for Federal Reserve assistance. Trump administration prepares largest mass visa revocation in U.S. history, targeting up to 200,000 people : The State Department is to revoke B1 and B2 business and tourism visas from up to 200,000 asylum seekers between 2016 to 2026, according to State Department documents obtained by the Associated Press, in what would be the largest single mass visa revocation in U.S. history. State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott said the department is "coordinating with DHS to identify and revoke the nonimmigrant visas of foreigners who have come to the United States claiming to be short-term visitors, but then file for asylum to stay here permanently." The revocations would not necessarily trigger immediate deportation, officials said, but would recategorize most pending asylum cases and strip holders of business or tourism status. Trump administration proposes new $103,000 H-1B visa fee after court struck down earlier version : The Trump administration a $103,265 fee for employers seeking H-1B skilled worker visas, according to a regulation posted Monday and reported by The Washington Post, taking a new legal approach after U.S. District Judge Leo T. Sorokin struck down a similar $100,000 fee in June. Unlike the administration's previous proposal, it would apply broadly to H-1B holders already in the U.S., not just new applicants from abroad. The regulation exempts some groups, including most U.S. colleges, universities, and nonprofit hospitals affiliated with academic institutions. The estimated $8.8 billion generated by the fee annually will fund federal immigration courts, ICE, and U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services, according to the regulation. U.S. partners with British firm to develop nuclear-powered merchant fleet, challenge China 's shipbuilding dominance: The Trump administration signed a public-private partnership agreement on Tuesday with the London-based company Core Power to accelerate development of a U.S.-flagged nuclear-powered commercial fleet, an agreement initially reported on by the Financial Times. A representative from the U.S. Maritime Administration cited the U.S.'s desire to counter Chinese shipping pre-eminence when discussing the deal, saying that the deal forwards U.S. plans to "compete on technology." Core Power, which has raised about $200 million from investors including Mitsui, Mitsubishi, and Sumitomo, plans to begin building its first nuclear-powered vessel in 2028. Supreme Court opens path for Trump mail voting restrictions ahead of midterms : The Supreme Court's conservative majority Monday that states suing to block President Donald Trump's executive order restricting mail-in voting lacked legal standing to challenge it, opening a path for the order's implementation without ruling on its legality. The order, signed in March, would require states to submit voter eligibility lists before USPS delivers mail ballots. Ballots are set to be mailed out as early as September 4, the date on which North Carolina will send its ballots to military and overseas voters. About 30% of 2024 ballots were cast by mail, according to federal data. The three liberal justices dissented, with Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson writing the ruling "lets another shoe drop in the Kafkaesque nightmare that our precedents have been steadily creating" for plaintiffs bringing election-related suits before the Court. IMEU poll shows Democratic voters overwhelmingly think Israel is committing genocide in Gaza: Across the first six states set to vote in the 2028 Democratic presidential primaries, the majority of likely Democratic voters say Israel is genocide in Gaza. Under 5% of Democratic voters believe Israel is not committing a genocide, according to YouGov polling reported by IMEU, though a sizeable number were unsure . Even in South Carolina, which recorded the lowest "yes" response, the divide is overwhelming: 57% said Israel is committing genocide against Palestinians, just 4% said it is not, and 39% were unsure. 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com Other International News 47 killed in Haiti in gang raid near capital: At least 47 people were and 22 wounded in a heavily armed gang raid on a neighborhood near Haiti's capital of Port-au-Prince, the UN reported on Monday, with homes set ablaze. The hillside farming community of Kenscoff has suffered numerous attacks by armed gangs since last year, forcing thousands to flee their homes. U.S. removes Syria from terrorism list: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio announced Monday that after nearly 47 years, Washington has formally removed Syria from its list of "State Sponsors of Terrorism." Rubio said the move is intended to "unlock new potential for Syria's economic revitalization and progress," marking another major step in the Trump administration's normalization of relations with the Al-Sharaa government in Damascus. The designation had subjected Syria to sweeping U.S. restrictions on foreign assistance, arms exports and financial transactions since December 1979, when the State Sponsors of Terrorism list was first created, and Syria was placed on it from the outset. The U.S. justification centered on the Syrian government's support and safe haven for Palestinian resistance groups and, later, Hezbollah. Investigative journalist and Drop Site News correspondent Ali Younes faces up to a year in prison in Jordan: On August 17, Younes, an American-Jordanian citizen, was and questioned by Jordanian intelligence officers on arrival at Queen Alia Airport, taken into custody, and later released with an order to appear before prosecutors in Amman. Younes and his lawyer have been informed that he has been accused of allegedly retweeting an article from the American Conservative that included a call to cut U.S. funding to Jordan, an act authorities are treating as the crime of "undermining the national security of Jordan." At a court hearing this week he was also informed that he had been charged with sedition and hate crimes in connection with the alleged retweet. Greece moves Patriot battery: Greece transferring a Patriot air-defense battery from the eastern island of Karpathos to Crete on Sunday, following reported Iranian threats against U.S. military targets in Europe. Euronews, citing Greek media, report that the system is being moved to the Souda military facility, home to the largest U.S. and NATO base in the eastern Mediterranean. Images showed the truck-mounted missile batteries at Karpathos's port awaiting transfer by barge. Greece's Defense Ministry had not publicly commented on the redeployment as of Monday, August 24. U.S. pushes nationwide Sudan arms embargo, criticizes unnamed "external actors": At Monday's UN Security Council briefing, Trump advisor Massad Boulos a draft resolution to expand the Darfur arms embargo across Sudan, explicitly include drones and related technology, enlarge the UN monitoring panel, and strengthen investigations of sanctions violations, ahead of the sanctions regime's September 12 renewal. The expansion would newly extend the embargo into SAF-held central and eastern Sudan. Russia opposed the move, while Sudan requested only a technical renewal of the existing Darfur regime, AFP reported. The briefing repeatedly placed the forces on equal footing. Boulos said the "brutality" of the SAF and RSF had discredited both, while UN political chief Rosemary DiCarlo blamed external support "to both parties," without criticizing the UAE for supporting the genocidal Raid Support Forces. body:
The next generation needs us.

---
| | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137890258/642292904/-507177811?refcode=EM_BS_LUR_260825_FR_VioletteRS_A0_na_U1_X2_M1&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MDA3OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzZmQ3NTBjZS05YmEwLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlmMWQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=Mwj2PQr8CR2oGeaCobwvRSDXPDzo4TBigPaTNnSQQ3k=)
When my daughter Violette was eight years old, I was running for Congress. I was proud to show her that women can do anything: raise kids, take on demanding careers, and make a real difference in the world. She's older now. She's bright, confident, and conscientious. But she's growing up in a country that is failing its young women. That makes me angry. It also makes me determined. The leaders who have failed America's women and girls have a lot to answer for. Reproductive rights stripped away. An economy that squeezes working moms and families while those at the top get richer. A future that feels uncertain. **As a mother, I refuse to accept that for Violette's generation.** I'm running to restore what's been taken. To make reproductive freedom the law of the land, not leave it to the whims of a court or a politician. To make sure girls today have the same opportunities I had at their age. I was proud to show her that women can do anything: raise kids, take on demanding careers, and make a real difference in the world. She's older now. She's bright, confident, and conscientious. But she's growing up in a country that is failing its young women. That makes me angry. It also makes me determined. The leaders who have failed America's women and girls have a lot to answer for. Reproductive rights stripped away. An economy that squeezes working moms and families while those at the top get richer. A future that feels uncertain. As a mother, I refuse to accept that for Violette's generation. I'm running to restore what's been taken. I'm going to make you a deal. I won't tell you the sky is falling. I won't pretend this is the last fundraising text or email you'll get from me. ## The Media Can't Even Let America Enjoy Its 250th Birthday
This summer, our country reached a historic milestone: 250 years of American independence, freedom, and constitutional democracy.
You'd think that 250 years of liberty, economic strength, and patriotism would be the one thing that everyone in this country could celebrate and be proud of together.
Think again.
[| | | | | Dr. Tanvi Sachar
---
@DrTanviSacharX
🔥 Democrats are absolutely LOSING IT over President Trump's Freedom 250 celebrations 😂 Why? Because Trump shut down their plans for a "medieval costume party" on the National Mall and replaced it with an actual celebration of America's 250th birthday 🇺🇸 Now they're melting
| 1:11 AM * Aug 24, 2026 * 558 Views6 Likes
---](https://substack.com/redirect/77b35806-216c-40d4-8ff2-ada1d81b0b48?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Instead of highlighting local parades, historic restorations, or the millions of families gathering on the National Mall to honor our founding, the mainstream media and left-wing critics did what they know best.
They turned a moment of national unity into a partisan weapon.
I've spent over 30 years in national politics and communications, and I've seen how the press handles major national milestones, going all the way back to how people talk about the Bicentennial in 1976.
The playbook hasn't changed, but the cynicism about our president and this incredible nation has hit an all-time high.
The bottom line is simple: if the left can't control the narrative, they'd rather tear down the celebration.
When everyday Americans look at the Semiquincentennial, they see the miracle of 1776, the bravery of Washington's army, and the enduring genius of our Constitution and our government's design.
When the mainstream media looks at it, they only want to talk about grievances and historical hand-wringing, boycotting the history that made our nation what it is today.
There is a stark difference between celebrating our country and finding every excuse to tear it down.
Let's get into it. ...

**The SC Legislature passed a budget. Communities lost the most with no earmarks.**
South Carolina state government has been operating under a continuing resolution since July 1 because the legislature was unable to finalize a spending plan before the start of the new fiscal year.
Budget writers set aside $377.7 million for lawmaker projects in a separate piece of legislation. They gave themselves a Sept. 30 deadline to allocate the money, but lawmakers would have had to come back in the fall to approve a supplemental spending bill, which risks the possibility of negative headlines on certain projects less than two months before the November election.
Budget negotiators had agreed to have a joint committee decide how much money each earmark received. That went out the window as budget writers tried to resolve earmark funding before Tuesday’s session, and communities are the ones who will lose the most.[ Read more here.](https://us.list-manage.com/tuvtVDwZsEK?e=edbde6c9b1&c2id=d580cd1bdfbc15e62e8fc86070aa989a)

We had a full week with our Run, Ladies, Run! Event that raised $7,500 to support getting out the vote this Fall and we attended the Spartanburg Rotary Club meeting with local candidates.
Mallory Dittmer for Congress hosted a town hall in Boiling Springs, Sylvia Wright for Superintendent of Education held a listening session for voters at Travelers Rest Baptist Church in Spartanburg, Irene Benson for House District 32 engaged with voters at the meet and greet in Converse Heights, and our candidates knocked doors on Saturday morning.
I had the pleasure of meeting with Pete Buttigieg in Columbia on Saturday before we hosted Dr. Annie Andrews at The Beacon on Sunday with an energetic crowd of supporters. Then I headed to Nashville to attend the pARTisan art exhibit and meet the incredible women building the TN Table...and I got to meet Anna Golladay who is running against a 30 year incumbent in Chattanooga.
Democracy is a participatory sport y’all, and it’s time to ramp up. Stay with me!

| | | | | | Peter,

**Election Day is just two weeks away...**

That means there is no time to sit on the sidelines. Every liberty-loving patriot needs to make a plan to vote, and then make sure the people around them are ready to do the same.

Mark your calendar. Talk to your family. Call your friends. Remind your neighbors and coworkers. Make sure everyone who shares New Hampshire’s commitment to freedom knows what is at stake and has a plan to show up.

**This primary election is our best shot at putting more Pledge Signers in position to fight for our rights in Concord.**

Our teams are out knocking on doors every single day to make sure we elect a legislature that actually represents the values of this state.

We are talking to voters face to face to build the momentum these candidates need to win, but we cannot do it alone...

One of the greatest privileges of representing El Paso in Congress is listening to our community's needs — and then fighting to deliver. Upgrading its infrastructure may not make national headlines, but it directly affects the safety and well-being of our community. Aging water and stormwater systems can threaten hospital access and operations during severe weather events, when our community needs reliable care most. clean_body: This is what it means to fight for El Paso in Congress. | | | | When you elected me to Congress, you trusted me to fight for El Paso and make sure our community receives its fair share of federal resources. I've always believed that effective representation means more than just having a seat at the table. It means using that seat to deliver tangible results for the people I represent. One of the greatest privileges of representing El Paso in Congress is listening to our community's needs — and then fighting to deliver. Last week, we had the opportunity to celebrate a win I'm incredibly proud of:I secured $1.1 million in federal funding for University Medical Center of El Paso (UMC) to replace aging water infrastructure and help protect critical hospital operations during severe weather. UMC is a lifeline for families across our region. Upgrading its infrastructure may not make national headlines, but it directly affects the safety and well-being of our community. Aging water and stormwater systems can threaten hospital access and operations during severe weather events, when our community needs reliable care most. These are the kinds of local investments I fight for every day. But with Election Day approaching, keeping this momentum going requires your help. Delivering for El Paso takes more than a single funding win — it requires having someone in Congress who will keep showing up, keep listening, and keep fighting for El Paso year after year. My name is Ron Barber.
#

[](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giff-em-q32026.gsDos-&refcode=em260825-1-b-nobox&t=29&akid=11760%2E3935704%2EZ1X5Fy)
---
Friends,
My name is Ron Barber, and in 2011, I almost died alongside Gabby Giffords.
January 8, 2011, was a brisk Saturday morning in Tucson, when Congresswoman Gabby Giffords arrived for her “Congress on your Corner” event. I was serving as her district director.
It was supposed to be just another Saturday. But in just 19.6 seconds, six people lay dying and 13 others were wounded when a gunman opened fire in front of a Safeway supermarket.
The gunman shot Gabby in the head — leaving her with a condition called aphasia. I was shot in the face and in the leg. I was fading and almost died on the ground. But I thought about my family and tried to keep my eyes open until we made it to the trauma center that saved my life.
**Fifteen years later, Gabby and I still carry the scars of that terrible day._Some days are harder than others, but we can never stop fighting._**
Gun violence is a uniquely American crisis. We’ve seen gun deaths increase dramatically in the past two decades, becoming more common than car crashes. And far too often, we see disturbing new reports of politically motivated gun violence when we turn on the TV.
That is simply unacceptable. We have the tools to fix this epidemic, but we need our elected leaders to have the courage to take on the gun lobby and defend our democracy.
_That’s why I am reaching out personally:_
The November elections are in less than 75 days, and everything is at stake. GIFFORDS is working to defeat extremist candidates and help gun safety champions win in the most competitive races. But Gabby needs our support to reach more voters.

Friend, With the rapid expansion of Flock safety cameras compromising our privacy right here in Tennessee, people are asking a very fair question: _**Where the Flock is Marsha Blackburn?**_ _****_ While our communities face a _massive wave of private surveillance tech_ , _**Senator Marsha Blackburn has been completely missing in action.**_ She avoids public town halls, only appears at carefully controlled publicity events, and when she is caught on camera, she's often seen _sprinting for the nearest exit_ to dodge any unscripted questions from voters and reporters. **Jerri Green knows _we can do a whole lot better._** While Marsha hides, _Jerri has been talking to Tennesseans every single day_ , traveling back and forth across the state,_meeting directly with constituents_ at over 150 stops and counting. As a Georgetown-trained criminal defense lawyer and Chief Public Defender for Shelby County, Jerri is commited to _making sure law enforcement officers have the tools they need_ to keep our communities and families safe. _**But she also knows that public safety can never be a blank check for mass surveillance.**_
### **Jerri Green’s Plan for Surveillance and Privacy**
* **Enact a State Moratorium:** Place an immediate pause on cameras operated by the state highway patrol or state police to allow for a comprehensive review of privacy concerns.
* **Establish Statewide Regulations** : Enact clear, mandatory rules governing automated license plate readers rather than relying on industry self-regulation.
* **Enforce Strict Data Retention Limits:** Cap the length of time vehicle detection data can be stored by law enforcement and private partners.
* **Control Data Access & Transparency:** Implement transparent standards regarding who is authorized to access surveillance data and under what circumstances.
* **Mandate Audits & Accountability: **Require rigorous, regular audits of surveillance systems with real, enforceable consequences for misuse.
* **Restrict Cross-Jurisdictional Sharing:** Place strict legal boundaries on sharing collected information outside the specific agency or local jurisdiction that gathered it.
* **Protect Our Constitutional Freedoms:** Uphold Fourth Amendment protections to ensure public safety initiatives respect boundaries on government power.

clean_body: | Friend, With the rapid expansion of Flock safety cameras compromising our privacy right here in Tennessee, people are asking a very fair question: Where the Flock is Marsha Blackburn? ** While our communities face a massive wave of private surveillance tech , Senator Marsha Blackburn has been completely missing in action. She avoids public town halls, only appears at carefully controlled publicity events, and when she is caught on camera, she's often seen sprinting for the nearest exit to dodge any unscripted questions from voters and reporters. Jerri Green knows we can do a whole lot better. While Marsha hides, Jerri has been talking to Tennesseans every single day , traveling back and forth across the state,meeting directly with constituents at over 150 stops and counting. As a Georgetown-trained criminal defense lawyer and Chief Public Defender for Shelby County, Jerri is commited to making sure law enforcement officers have the tools they need to keep our communities and families safe. But she also knows that public safety can never be a blank check for mass surveillance. Jerri Green’s Plan for Surveillance and Privacy Enact a State Moratorium: Place an immediate pause on cameras operated by the state highway patrol or state police to allow for a comprehensive review of privacy concerns. Establish Statewide Regulations : Enact clear, mandatory rules governing automated license plate readers rather than relying on industry self-regulation. Enforce Strict Data Retention Limits: Cap the length of time vehicle detection data can be stored by law enforcement and private partners. Control Data Access & Transparency: Implement transparent standards regarding who is authorized to access surveillance data and under what circumstances. Mandate Audits & Accountability: Require rigorous, regular audits of surveillance systems with real, enforceable consequences for misuse. Restrict Cross-Jurisdictional Sharing: Place strict legal boundaries on sharing collected information outside the specific agency or local jurisdiction that gathered it. Protect Our Constitutional Freedoms: Uphold Fourth Amendment protections to ensure public safety initiatives respect boundaries on government power. As governor, Jerri will use state grant and funding controls to enforce oversight and compliance across the board. Tennesseans deserve a leader who shows up in person and fights for what matters most: privacy, safety, quality public education, affordable healthcare, and a living wage. Tennesseans deserve that — not someone whose run is fueled by dark money and culture war grievances. As governor, Jerri Green will fight to keep Tennesseans safe from criminals and safe from government overreach.We don’t have to choose between our safety and our privacy. Marsha Blackburn's policies are unpopular, but her pockets are deep and packed with money from corporate donors. To beat her and her billionaire backers, we've been building a well oiled, grassroots powered machine,fueled by you.= If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | | = = | = = | = = Thanks so much for standing with Jerri in this fight. Julie Roginsky came on Tequila Talk with a story almost nobody in American media was touching: for the better part of a week, NATO has been massing serious force around Kaliningrad, and no one will explain why.
* The buildup nobody will explain. Polish ground troops, British naval power, Danish forces, and United States Air Force aircraft, including a platform that just came online. Not a scheduled exercise. NATO has offered no reason at all.

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/6931f241-ee11-4eb6-877d-b409b857a68c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* Roginsky's theory, and she calls it a theory. There is a run on Russian banks and gas lines in Moscow. The war has finally reached the people Putin spent three years protecting from it. What does a cornered leader do about that?
* The probes nobody added up. Drones into Poland and Romania. An airport shut down in Denmark. Von der Leyen's plane losing GPS. A bomb at Leipzig that did not go off. Julie walks the pattern and names the next target...

| | | Fellow Patriot, I need to be honest with you about where this race stands. See above. Cash is king, but in a major Senate race like ours cash-on-hand (meaning, money in our bank account that we can spend) is king... _And the numbers are looking bad ..._ **Right now, James Talarico has $21.5 million cash on hand in the bank. We have $6.9 million cash on hand.** That gap is serious, and it matters -- because right now, today, he is on television in nearly every major market in Texas and we cannot answer him... Cash on hand is not a political talking point. It is the difference between being heard and being drowned out. Every dollar given today will have a massive impact... And every dollar ungiven widens the gap and increases the Democrats' chances for unleashing chaos... **On top of that ...**Three separate polls show this race tied. Cook Political Report just downgraded us. The national media is starting to write the story they want to write... _We cannot let them write it. We need to change the narrative now!_ This race is decided right now, in the next 72 hours, by people like you who decide whether to step up or sit it out... **_Will you help right now?_** Remember, I have spent my career fighting for Texas. I have gone up against the federal government, the open border lobby, and the entire weight of the Washington establishment -- _and I have not backed down once_. Team,The Supreme Court dropped another "shadow docket" ruling last night, this one **making it easier for Trump to implement his anti-mail-in voting Executive Order**.First: The "_shadow docket_." It's the Supreme Court's way to review cases quickly without formal hearings. It's a construct of the last few decades, not widely used previous to that, but tons of unsigned, pro-Trump rulings have been issued from the Supreme Court this way the last few years. This ruling, _offered on procedural grounds and not the merits of the law_ , was a short-term win for the Trump administration as they try to **use the Department of Homeland Security and the Postal Service to create a national voter registration list and usurp the constitutional authority of the states to run our elections**. Even if this is short-lived, **this is not good news.** Opponents of voting rights will take every inch they can in their battle to suppress votes and invalidate your ballot. | | | We can't say it any better than Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson's dissent: “ _This ruling violates well-established precedents concerning this Court’s equitable discretion and**needlessly injects chaos and uncertainty into the upcoming midterm elections**. It also lets another shoe drop in the Kafkaesque nightmare that our precedents have been steadily creating for certain plaintiffs who seek to bring election-related challenges. The Court has held for a while now that even valid election-related legal claims can come too late. Today’s revelation is that such claims can also come too early—**never mind that an election is looming and related harms**_ _**are presently occurring**. Never mind, too, that the Government (which controls the timing of proposed and final rules) can easily game the system_.” While this ruling didn't render a verdict on the merits of Trump's executive order, the Court’s decision still overrules a series of lower federal court rulings blocking that order, which represents **an unprecedented attempt by the Trump administration to seize constitutional control of election administration from the states** , based on Trump’s demands for his party to “nationalize the voting” and “take over” the voting systems in a partisan fashion. **Why this case, and why now?** From the complaint brought by 23 states from across the country: “ _Because of t**he high risk of errors and the limited window for correcting mistakes** , many of the millions of voters who rely on mail voting—especially voters with disabilities and those in rural areas—**would likely be denied mail ballots and, as a result, disenfranchised**. clean_body: Mother Jones: SCOTUS hands Trump a temporary win in his crusade against mail voting| | | | | | | | | = Team,The Supreme Court dropped another "shadow docket" ruling last night, this one making it easier for Trump to implement his anti-mail-in voting Executive Order.First: The "shadow docket." It's the Supreme Court's way to review cases quickly without formal hearings. It's a construct of the last few decades, not widely used previous to that, but tons of unsigned, pro-Trump rulings have been issued from the Supreme Court this way the last few years. This ruling, offered on procedural grounds and not the merits of the law , was a short-term win for the Trump administration as they try to use the Department of Homeland Security and the Postal Service to create a national voter registration list and usurp the constitutional authority of the states to run our elections. Even if this is short-lived, this is not good news. Opponents of voting rights will take every inch they can in their battle to suppress votes and invalidate your ballot. The harder we make it to vote, the more politicians make voter participation feel worthless, the less people actually take part, and the less our democracy and our government looks like the people it's supposed to represent. = | | | = | | = | | | = | | = | | | = | | = | | | We can't say it any better than Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson's dissent: “ This ruling violates well-established precedents concerning this Court’s equitable discretion andneedlessly injects chaos and uncertainty into the upcoming midterm elections. It also lets another shoe drop in the Kafkaesque nightmare that our precedents have been steadily creating for certain plaintiffs who seek to bring election-related challenges. The Court has held for a while now that even valid election-related legal claims can come too late. Today’s revelation is that such claims can also come too early—never mind that an election is looming and related harms are presently occurring. Never mind, too, that the Government (which controls the timing of proposed and final rules) can easily game the system.” While this ruling didn't render a verdict on the merits of Trump's executive order, the Court’s decision still overrules a series of lower federal court rulings blocking that order, which represents an unprecedented attempt by the Trump administration to seize constitutional control of election administration from the states , based on Trump’s demands for his party to “nationalize the voting” and “take over” the voting systems in a partisan fashion. Why this case, and why now? From the complaint brought by 23 states from across the country: “ Because of the high risk of errors and the limited window for correcting mistakes , many of the millions of voters who rely on mail voting—especially voters with disabilities and those in rural areas—would likely be denied mail ballots and, as a result, disenfranchised. Many more voters would be confused—either because they wouldn’t receive their mail ballots or would fear that USPS would fail to deliver their voted ballots to state officials for tabulation.” = | | | | | | | ---|---|---|--- Integrity First Voter Action Project is dedicated to expanding ballot access and increasing voter participation across the country. Since the Supreme Court gutted key provisions in the Voting Rights Act, extreme politicians have taken advantage to pass harsh laws that restrict access to the ballot box. These restrictions particularly affect disadvantaged communities and people of color. Peter, After Republicans gerrymandered me out of Congress, I had a choice. As a former congressman I could have made a boatload of money lobbying, and plenty go do exactly that. Instead I looked at our open Senate seat against Thom Tillis and thought: that’s a fight worth having. So I ran. I gave it everything I had, because I love our state and I wasn’t going to sit on the sidelines with Trump shredding the Constitution in the Oval Office. Then Thom Tillis got out and Roy Cooper got in, and I had another decision to make. I could have stayed in and fought Roy for the nomination. Two Democrats trading punches for a year while Trump takes a wrecking ball to our democracy? Or I could get out of the way to give Roy the best possible shot at winning the seat. **I got out of the way.** And here’s why. I always thought Roy would be the strongest candidate we could put up, period. Two-term governor. Four-term attorney general. Six statewide wins, zero losses. **If you built a candidate in a lab to flip North Carolina blue, you’d build Roy Cooper.** [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137895769/642311592/1289741405?email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&refcode=AU_GWN_FR_TAN_GEN_AC_20260825_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84ODMxNCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1MGNkMzI4OC1hNWEwLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlmMWQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=AHV4yAvl17I2BUAPr6J4TVB-NN2vI9xXhuk8y-Y2ziA=) So I didn’t just get out of the way. I went all in to get him elected. I didn’t just endorse with a press release and a retweet. The week I dropped out, I rolled up my sleeves and organized a fundraiser for Roy at my home in Cary. Endorsing him was never the point. Getting him elected was. Here’s the hard truth. Since 1986, Democrats have won a Senate race in North Carolina exactly twice. Two times in forty years. And now MAGA Republicans are about to dump an ungodly pile of dark money on this state to keep the streak alive. But here’s what’s real: **the Cook Political Report just moved this race to lean Democrat and called it the GOP seat Democrats are most likely to flip in the entire country.** So here’s my ask. Do what I did. name: Jamie Davis
subject: Dolly Parton’s death has left me with a heavy heart
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Jamie Davis for U
body:
Dolly was more than a country music legend. She was a daughter of the rural South who never forgot where she came from. She championed the poor, the marginalized, and the forgotten with grace, humor,
| | | | |
---
| My heart is heavy today.
I'm Jamie Davis -- Democratic nominee for Senate in Louisiana. And like so many of you, I'm mourning the loss of a true American treasure: Dolly Parton.
Dolly was more than a country music legend. She was a daughter of the rural South who never forgot where she came from.
She fought for universal literacy and education through her Imagination Library. She championed the poor, the marginalized, and the forgotten with grace, humor, and boundless love.
---
|
---
| As someone who grew up in rural Louisiana -- not far from Dolly's world in spirit if not in miles -- her story always moved me deeply. We both know what it means to come from nothing and fight for something bigger than yourself.
The greatest tribute we can pay to Dolly Parton is to keep fighting for the people she spent her whole life fighting for.
Rest easy, Dolly. You will always be loved.
--Jamie Davis
---
---

name: Swing Left
subject: NEW TARGETS
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Swing Left, [swingleft
body:
#
Hi there,
**Today, we’re announcing an expansion of our 2026 target list, adding 11 new U.S. House districts and 3 new U.S. Senate races—and moving 11 House districts, 2 Senate races, and 2 Governor’s races from our “Reach” category to “Must-Flip” or “Must-Hold.”**
[](https://act.swingleft.org/go/27?c0=sl-balance-of-power-2026.KwVigu&refcode=em20260825-2565&t=1&akid=2565%2E1562180%2EqFOarl)
We’re making this decision now because the political environment continues to move in Democrats’ direction. Those changes are putting races on the map that we wouldn’t normally expect to be competitive, including historically red states like Texas, Iowa, and Mississippi.
Recent polling shows Donald Trump’s approval rating at just 33%, making him historically unpopular as he faces mounting voter backlash over the ongoing Iran war and a growing affordability crisis heading into the November midterm elections. Combined with Republicans’ politically toxic agenda and the strong Democratic turnout we’ve seen throughout this primary season, more candidates and districts are becoming genuinely competitive.
But we’re not adding races simply because the overall environment looks better.
We take a ruthlessly pragmatic and data-driven approach to deciding where the Swing Left community can make the biggest difference. We look at things like polling, fundraising, past election results, and turnout patterns as well as talk directly with campaigns to assess their operations and with local leaders to see where there’s untapped organizing potential. Even still, we are tracking new races on our map that are going to be big reaches—and while we might not win them all, signals are pointing to potentially very strong election results for Democrats in November.
What we’re seeing and hearing is what’s led to this target refresh:
* **Defending against more Republican redistricting efforts:** Republican gerrymandering in Florida earlier this year changed the map and made races like Florida’s 9th, 14th, and 25th Congressional Districts more competitive, but strong Democratic incumbents and past election results are putting these districts on our map.

* **New polling and fundraising numbers are showing Democratic strength:** In races like Colorado’s 5th Congressional District, the Texas Senate race, and the Iowa Governor’s race, Democrats are polling ahead of or within striking distance of their Republican opponents. And Democrats in races like South Carolina’s 1st Congressional District and Virginia’s 5th Congressional District are outraising their Republican opponents, putting them in a better position to communicate with and turn out the voters they need to win.

* **Some Republican candidates are increasingly vulnerable:** In Ohio’s 7th Congressional District, for example, Rep. Max Miller is facing allegations of domestic violence and calls from prominent Republicans to end his campaign, creating a rare opening for a Democratic challenger.

* **And we’re following volunteer energy, too:** New York’s 1st Congressional District has an active Swing Left volunteer base that’s ready to engage immediately in this newly added “reach” race. They’re already seeing what’s possible here—the impact of Trump’s and Republicans’ policies is turning this district, where Trump won by just 2% in 2020, purple again.

We continue to categorize our target races into Must-Flip, Must-Hold, or Reach Races.
**Must-Flip** and **Must-Hold** races are the highest-priority races on our list. These are the races that Democrats must win to gain control of the House or Senate, or hold critical power in the states.
**Reach** races are more of a stretch based on past results, current polling, or the partisan makeup of the district or state. Targeting some of these races is very ambitious, but they are also a key part of our long-term strategy, too. Organizing investment in these places now could result in an extra seat, and if we don’t win a race this November, Democrats build groundwork that will make it easier to win next time around.
We take seriously what it means to ask you for your time and money. That’s why right now, we are focusing the Swing Left community’s power on organizing in these Reach races rather than fundraising. This moment requires us to be clear-eyed about the work to win these races and the investment it requires, and we know that any chance at winning starts with building organizing power on the ground. And even if we don’t win this November, the work we start now will have a lasting impact, building up a volunteer infrastructure that will outlast a single election cycle.
Our goal remains ensuring your time and money go where they’ll have the biggest impact on helping Democrats not only win in the midterm elections, but to build a foundation to win and maintain Democratic governing power in 2028, 2030, and beyond. [**If you’d like to see the full list of target races, you can find it here!**](https://act.swingleft.org/go/1219?utm_source=em20260825-2565&t=2&akid=2565%2E1562180%2EqFOarl)
We’re putting our collective grassroots power to work in two main ways. First, through **Ground Truth** , our innovative voter-contact program helping Democrats reach the voters who will decide these races. And second, through **building a grassroots fundraising machine** that directs small-dollar donations to candidates where they'll make the biggest difference, with a particular focus on flipping Republican-held seats blue.
The Swing Left community has proven in the past that grassroots dollars have the power to make a difference in close races, and now we’re aiming to replicate that success on a much larger scale than ever before.
[**One of the best ways to take action right now is by making a donation to Swing Left’s Balance of Power Fund to directly support Democrats in our Must-Flip House races and our Must-Win Senate races.** ](https://act.swingleft.org/go/27?c0=sl-balance-of-power-2026.KwVigu&refcode=em20260825-2565&t=3&akid=2565%2E1562180%2EqFOarl)
**[Donate Now](https://act.swingleft.org/go/27?c0=sl-balance-of-power-2026.KwVigu&refcode=em20260825-2565&t=4&akid=2565%2E1562180%2EqFOarl)**
With Election Day just 10 weeks away, campaigns are hiring last-minute staff, building up voter-contact programs, holding supporter events, and reserving ad space to communicate directly with voters. Momentum might be on their side, but that momentum will mean nothing if campaigns don’t have the resources to capitalize on it now.
Thank you for all you’re doing to help Democrats win, and keep winning. And stay tuned for more updates on our new target races soon!
— The Swing Left Team

**Since 2017, Swing Left has channeled the energy of grassroots volunteers and donors to elect Democrats, up and down the ballot, focusing on the most competitive races that can swing the national balance of power.** Right now, Swing Left is investing in grassroots organizing in key swing districts and initiatives across the country to flip the House and win the Senate and critical states in 2026. [**If you’d like to help support our work, you can make a donation using this link.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_sl_footer?refcode=em20260825-1&t=5&refcode2=2565_1562180_qFOarl&akid=2565%2E1562180%2EqFOarl)
