clean_body: We’re the richest country in the world. We can afford to take care of our mothers.| | | | = It’s completely outrageous that in 2026, millions of American women and pregnant people have to drive long distances to access essential, basic care. = A new report found that more than a third of all U.S. counties are considered maternity care deserts — meaning for too many women, there are no hospitals, birthing centers, or obstetrics clinics where they live. But that’s not all. More than half of all U.S. counties don't have a hospital with labor and delivery services, and nearly 70% of those maternity care deserts are in rural counties — forcing individuals to drive burdensome long distances to access care. Women’s reproductive health care has been under constant attack over the last decade, drastically increasing the number of care deserts. When Roe v. Wade was overturned, red states passed abortion bans and laws that criminalized providers and patients, and OBGYNs everywhere have had to make difficult choices. Case in point: In Idaho, more than a third of OBGYNs have left the state since Roe was overturned. And then you have the federal government with Donald Trump and Republicans at the helm. → They’ve defunded Planned Parenthood and abortion providers, which has caused dozens of health care clinics across the country to close. → They cut health care funding, which has led to more Americans going uninsured and small rural hospitals having to shut their doors. → Now, maternal and infant mortality are on the rise. And the richest country in the world is telling pregnant people and new mothers: you're on your own. I call bullsht. All of this is a direct result of policy choices — and Republicans just keep making it worse. The Big Ugly Bill signed into law last summer makes drastic cuts to Medicaid and creates new barriers that will push more people off their coverage entirely. But that’s not enough for Republicans. Mike Johnson said on the record a few weeks ago that Republicans plan to make even more cuts to Americans' health care in 2027! Trump and Republicans have chosen to let women suffer rather than fund their care. Let’s not give them that choice next year. =** If you’ve saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | = | = ---|--- = | = = | = | | | We are the richest country in the world. clean_body: Friends, Kathy Hochul lied to your face. She sold congestion pricing as a clean air miracle. Now the city's own Health Department has admitted the truth. Air quality was stable or improved slightly, a trend already two decades old, toll or no toll. | Friends, Kathy Hochul lied to your face. She sold congestion pricing as a clean air miracle. Now the city's own Health Department has admitted the truth. Air quality was stable or improved slightly, a trend already two decades old, toll or no toll. | The pitch was never about clean air. It was a con to bankroll a broken agency. That agency is the MTA, a black hole of cost overruns, delays, and mismanagement. It is now cashing $550 million a year of your money while riders eat breakdowns and unreliable service. Where is Comptroller Thomas DiNapoli? Nineteen years in office, and his answer to a toll built on a lie is a pat on the back for the MTA's books. Zero accountability for how the money gets spent. Hochul lied. DiNapoli looked away. New Yorkers got fleeced. When I am elected, this scam ends on Day One. | I will audit where the money is going, expose the waste and cost overruns, hold contractors accountable, and refuse to approve bad deals that stick New Yorkers with the bill. But I cannot do it without you. | | | | | Thank you, Joseph Hernandez Republican for NYS Comptroller P.S. They are betting you forget this by next week. Every dollar you give proves them wrong. | | Hernandez for New York, 697 3rd Avenue, #106, New York, NY 10017

This movement is not about partisan labels or purity tests. It is about class solidarity.
**It's about the thousands of you who stand together and say our lives deserve dignity, and our work deserves respect.**
It will never be just institutions and officials alone that uphold our democracy. It will always be the people — the masses who refuse to comply with authoritarian regimes — who are the last and strongest defense of our country and our freedoms.
We are at a crossroads: oligarchy or democracy. But we cannot have both.
**I've made my choice. We must fight the oligarchy that has created this nightmare.**

Now let me tell you why this mission means so much to me. My name is Eduardo Verastegui. Several years ago, I learned firsthand about the horrific reality of child trafficking. What I heard broke my heart. Children were being bought and sold.
Families were being torn apart.
Lives were being destroyed. **I couldn't forget it.** **I couldn't stay silent.** I kept asking myself one question: **"What if it were my child?"** That question changed my life. What started as a film project became a mission and a calling. That calling eventually led me to help produce the film _Sound of Freedom_. **Not for fame.**
**Not for awards.**
**But because I believed people needed to see the truth.** For years, many people said the film would never succeed. Doors closed.
Studios walked away.
People told us to give up. **But when innocent children are suffering, silence is not an option.** And while the film helped awaken millions of people to this crisis, awareness alone is not enough. That is why we created the **Sound of Freedom Foundation**. Our mission is simple: **To stop the sale of God's children.**

When you make your first gift to the Sound of Freedom Foundation today, we'll send you a FREE white "God's Children Are Not For Sale" t-shirt as our thank-you. | | | | | | | | This isn't a shirt you'll find in a store. Please accept this shirt as our way of saying thank you for joining this mission. Give any amount today and choose your shirt size and select a color. Now let me tell you why this mission means so much to me. My name is Eduardo Verastegui. Several years ago, I learned firsthand about the horrific reality of child trafficking. What I heard broke my heart. Children were being bought and sold. Families were being torn apart. Lives were being destroyed. I couldn't forget it. I couldn't stay silent. I kept asking myself one question: "What if it were my child?" That question changed my life. What started as a film project became a mission and a calling. That calling eventually led me to help produce the film Sound of Freedom. Not for fame. Not for awards. But because I believed people needed to see the truth. body:
| | | Welcome back to the WFP newsletter, Peter! We’ve got a lot to celebrate this month. WFP champions are winning big from Michigan to Florida, our state parties are growing, and working people are showing once again that no amount of billionaire money can substitute for a movement of people who are organized and ready to fight for each other. Of course, the billionaires seem determined to test that theory. They’re pouring millions into races across the country to stop our candidates and protect the status quo (which means we must be doing something right). So, let’s get into what WFP members have been up to this month — **the wins, the fights, and everything we’re building together.**
* * *
**_WFP SWEEP IN MICHIGAN_** **Our winning streak continued in Michigan this month, where our brand-new WFP chapter celebrated a**** _clean_****sweep of our federal candidates.** [](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqvlwhslwHzsYo7bshL1ic1bkV4PRhnH7RZF3DENncgqjw6v_TQFaag0JmD_5KPzWonbDX6yT5VX2uklQBZCeDqvHez63jCve_rqjRm2ioBxAo2CBJzVnRkQu7HKGoW60QCOD93f6e2673eK_OXCRFTcxaDRNFY0cqUEpTPtQ8eEZlLh0SjaeZPGMXcBMZAXY87fBzrJy-svKANVrPLXHKk2GRAYdNGmWtrvbenKlBkeR-1GCBwxbCtOC7cSWX-ETI1GtD6xCdnZdglCtIkSGDYox9wWY9QvoehZczuvYFpf-SmtIVIJtlGwYAHAhl00CxDzURkWv6_YwI96I6fSUPHS/4th/QuDbqUKjRRyRQRpc1Mng-A/h0/h001.Yd8JbfAoaR16seGbAlI6lJSteGbCbOLA9TR3BlQGX4o) **** Public health expert **Abdul El-Sayed** won his primary for U.S. Senate, Sunrise Movement co-founder and WFP member **Will Lawrence** won in the 7th Congressional District, and WFP State Rep. **Donavan McKinney** won in the 13th District. All three ran on a bold agenda of guaranteed health care and child care, good union jobs, and taking on the corporations and AI oligarchs exploiting our communities. And the billionaire class certainly tried to stop them. **Abdul faced more outside spending than**** _any_****other Senate primary candidate in U.S. history** — and won anyway. Turns out money can buy a lot of ads, but it can’t always buy an election. The wins also continued locally, with **Chris Gilmer-Hill** unseating a State House incumbent backed by utility money, **Abbas Alawieh** winning an open State Senate primary with a multiracial economic populist coalition, and **Yousef Rabhi** winning his primary for Ann Arbor Mayor on an economic justice platform. Michigan is part of a _growing_ wave of WFP victories across the country, as working people prove that organized people can beat organized money. [**If you’re ready to keep this momentum going and elect more working-class champions up and down the ballot this November, make a contribution to WFP today to help power the fights ahead.**](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqvlwhslwHzsYo7bshL1ic1bkV4PRhnH7RZF3DENncgqjw6v_TQFaag0JmD_5KPzWonbDX6yT5VX2uklQBZCeDqvpt_rIPNaaxjo92kmhjy2cpUfCr57iazNHA7LB_Si2g1PWccXEYzo7MfxqxGU6dPWUFUMPf7FFEtBE_w_wuY4kUClva_HE19T7Ro0RM-iR7KxmJ6UprPR-3_AeMmnKVNOUD2ss0dLtl98KKivaPiN944bNwAUOZB2_nf2hvn9yq9bTPfIJ0DWiK52fjxt_02ZpPb0uHhho5ypxM5sg6Mgv_tNfVqcpWCReeCbPDVKPkK4XjzisC1-g2_Gkp4fvXuw/4th/QuDbqUKjRRyRQRpc1Mng-A/h1/h001.7Y5A3gm2FnOW-WCWiaUnsZFVm1pFRd99pH5BmF28ViE)
* * *
**_ANGIE NIXON PROVES THEM WRONG IN FLORIDA_** From Michigan, our winning streak headed south — where WFP champion **Angie Nixon** scored a major victory in Florida. [](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfquqxZ_WMtWQ5nsYnjR236T9ixVkNAC3gdeerpvGOTXIZq2RDA7T-OB93vOBqsZ6a3bbIt85IueI8ouft1emPvswq0SoYqZOaLDJYtKyzwOgb6uwhcGYAy_2tMEVMv2vuYAZwR2DOF4e0HQpcYLrydTahd3shEqv9bFttSa9jrQCm8znp0wA10zIs7A7Q3CZMTz5t6Z4V-quyCt3PYEqWZWxwASySOuSaLWHKZgulSUKl44_WoMqhyiS_AZ43ykzuqb5ftxFYL4JJkGy8VlTd9F3jQVquyOWmUWZ0hcQG75M2YlnQzmm1L2tjtupKXl5TSs0jxOPPrz6oM0_0P0hPehN7VwjDLHwMDWbkkz5f7fNFQ/4th/QuDbqUKjRRyRQRpc1Mng-A/h2/h001.SdrnwhjwDo-K2eRAEDQ94lyPUwjYnvTKveMocRvEx7U) Angie won her primary for **U.S. Senate** with more than **700,000 votes** , despite being dramatically outspent by her opponent. A WFP member, labor organizer, community advocate, small-business owner, state lawmaker, and mother, Angie ran a campaign rooted in the **Working Families Guarantee** : health care you can count on, housing you can afford, child care when you need it, good jobs with livable wages, and a government that answers to everyday people — not billionaire bosses. **The political establishment may have thought a working-class candidate like Angie couldn’t win. Florida voters had other ideas.** Her decisive victory showed what we’ve long known: the South is hungry for change, and when we invest in working-class champions who speak directly to what people need, we can win. **Now comes the bigger fight. Angie is headed to the general election, and the corporate interests lining up against her will have plenty more money to spend.** [**We got Angie through the primary. Now, help us finish the job and send her to the U.S. Senate by splitting a contribution between Angie’s campaign and WFP today.**](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfquqxZ_WMtWQ5nsYnjR236T9ixVkNAC3gdeerpvGOTXIZq2RDA7T-OB93vOBqsZ6a3bbIt85IueI8ouft1emPvswBYq0YAvQpL7lmRdAfDq_bYpyKzJ3dlhhlO1s47Q_f37Mfo6UXZniJCzMSlJVz6qzFtUUvYmizR4Qa2Bg9hwG5RXUZVu6TqjUJIHhELF_OkC2MUu5uO5cVi7jL4KiAXvkY0KD_wsR5DLaJ3Re_PGgBatEHryKAdpQN02lkWcfjRwKdTgVremTNHs_MeadpVrOMJxWfH2IUDuk11pRqMGMLfhjkXv7rpFLre1CG3Q-io-8TgYthlG2toGvERxGmT0_5yEwL23Viq_v8JtIuGg9sw/4th/QuDbqUKjRRyRQRpc1Mng-A/h3/h001.ZIsNLrPOX5tgDgls4TLfe4oRlfCxhdydazd5JqiX51I)
* * *
**_PEOPLE POWER > NEW MAPS IN TENNESSEE_** **Florida wasn’t the only place in the South where working people made their voices heard this month.** In Tennessee, WFP champion **Justin J. Pearson** won the Democratic primary in the newly redrawn 9th Congressional District — on the 61st anniversary of the signing of the Voting Rights Act. [](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqvlwhslwHzsYo7bshL1ic1bkV4PRhnH7RZF3DENncgqjw6v_TQFaag0JmD_5KPzWonbDX6yT5VX2uklQBZCeDqvDixNBAhXhx4c67lwwsINN6BXLtChicdtwkzYAWi3xliODrOogLoX0hdI58UncAezMlf-kvO7bzCD3ZY7vjuGw-jU7cDIHs4z2v6Ba3uq1AUr8XcV7snzdwH1KXrltusSGsIyvthmsZkyRnNtMSSDU1ZXGUd15rtJgQl2_JYADY_SjpW170i-_qHKFdNTLxnMRWVouXWn8EHHClEGHzA2n9sj4O_aF5tLmzUzLt73o5wAW08SKy_Dke6Lmk1NSgLP/4th/QuDbqUKjRRyRQRpc1Mng-A/h4/h001.WkCChfJH9s3o5j6j7LvzxM-NyMXy_DWbZAuvYNb1Tp4)The timing couldn’t have been more fitting. Republicans _drastically_ redrew Tennessee’s last majority-Black congressional district, turning a compact Memphis-based seat into a sprawling, Republican-leaning district stretching roughly 200 miles. But Justin — one of the **Tennessee Three** , who was expelled from the State House after protesting for gun safety — knows a thing or two about what happens when politicians try to silence the people. **He defeated a State Senator backed by the local Democratic establishment and will now face a Trump-endorsed Republican this November.** Republicans may have drawn themselves a new map. Now, we’re organizing to make sure working people have the final say.
* * *
**_A HISTORIC WIN IN CALIFRONIA_** **California** officially joined this month’s win column, with a historic victory of its own, Peter. WFP-backed State Senator **Aisha Wahab** won the special election in California’s 14th Congressional District, making history as the **first Afghan American elected to Congress**. Aisha has taken on Wall Street landlords and corporate utilities and fought for affordable housing, workers, and working families — a record that drew **_millions_****in outside spending from AIPAC-linked groups** determined to stop her. But even after all that spending, Aisha came out on top. She’ll serve through January 2027, completing the remainder of Eric Swalwell’s term. **But this fight is far from over: Aisha will face her opponent again this November, this time for a full two-year term in Congress.** And the same forces that tried to stop her this time aren’t going anywhere. **But neither are we.**
* * *
**_THE WINNING STREAK CONTINUES_** **The summer winning streak made a stop in Arizona, too,** where WFP’s bloc in the state legislature is poised to grow after Democratic primary victories from **Lisbeth Arescurenaga, Miranda Lopez, and Alberto Flores**. And Arizona wasn’t alone: in **Connecticut, Maryam Khan, Jack Fazzino, Moise Carelus, Toni Lombardi, and Angie Parkinson** pulled off a clean sweep of their state legislative primaries, while across the country in **Washington State, Jaelynn Scott and Kelabe Tewolde** won their state legislative primaries and longtime organizer **Nilu Jenks** won her primary for Seattle City Council District 5. But we’re not done yet, Peter! **Massachusetts** heads to the polls on **September 1st** , where WFP has endorsed a slate of eight working-class champions for the state legislature: **Latoya Gayle, Carey McDonald, Daniel Lander, Lorena Betts, John Drinkwater, Tara Hong, Johnnie McKnight, and Celina Reyes.** They’re union members, educators, organizers, and local leaders running to take on business as usual on Beacon Hill and put working families first. **[From city councils to state legislatures, we’re building WFP power everywhere — and we plan to keep this winning streak going. Chip in today to help us keep the momentum going.](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqvlwhslwHzsYo7bshL1ic1bkV4PRhnH7RZF3DENncgqjw6v_TQFaag0JmD_5KPzWonbDX6yT5VX2uklQBZCeDqvGjnlXTZjv_af9L3J56snhphhMxk1bl0R_O3HHpOwgxy0F677MP8y6XTxsR0xK9HyykMf8GgAKLRLBTcS_5L63JvLTDXZliBQaMOf08E9HQns9Xeu7Ch4M0bGwW65SwIYXZf0zYvgzM0C69PS8dhQRF8nZjGld0oePOZvmx0r4LxOrelUenEaRTygV3s88jKYHlJ7zjB-CQaMRLCaMA4N2lRsBV1CTk7FaAJ-RWyLaa_ZRHIWuJSG1bnqRO6ABJNK/4th/QuDbqUKjRRyRQRpc1Mng-A/h5/h001.TgIujUmGojlB4_gBb9cxLPwdqRTMVxFX91SrdDL8pD4)**
* * *
**_ELON MUSK VS. WFP_** Apparently, WFP has gotten under the skin of the world’s richest man. Last year, Delaware legislators passed the controversial **“Billionaire’s Bill,”** handing massive giveaways to Elon Musk — who was apparently in desperate need of _another_ $56 billion — and other ultra-wealthy corporate shareholders. **Now, WFP is backing a slate of working families champions challenging legislators who supported the bill, and Musk’s corporate allies are fighting back.** Corporate law firms and their allies are pouring more than **$1 million** through super PACs and nonprofits into Delaware legislative races to protect incumbents who backed the Billionaire’s Bill. One donor is even the same firm Musk and Tesla used while the legislation was under consideration. That’s an _extraordinary_ amount of money for these races — and a pretty good indication that our challenges have them nervous. **This is exactly the kind of corporate power WFP is organizing to take on. If billionaires and their lawyers want to spend a fortune trying to stop us, they’re welcome to try.**
* * *
**_BUILDING THE PARTY_** Taking on billionaire power requires building some serious people power of our own — and that’s exactly what WFP members have been doing across the country. California WFP recently held its [**largest state convention ever**](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMWn3R7U15hZOprFI75oZg46vR29AxcOXFXAc3BlHIJ6KaW0WHpWFFVs_61QSznbG_yZyNkz_7cNFvPeO0f0X96reVl7H2S8uQ7h7zsNgQSx-4oUoutTr-DIIM9SAlM5q4exOK3iknV2ta-dGwhHg8DBgihKL_XLCvSzeNjOWUdzL254i2Gks9oyV-GqUrzslrTJzchm6DYm-VbdskLae9ze3PFcFzG4LgTgcNjO2vs4TQ22hSDR4lAdDdEeJf0oscQ/4th/QuDbqUKjRRyRQRpc1Mng-A/h6/h001.h8JYKdSa0Jbtu4owRAe3qBAqriFmZewPkSvG28jP2FU), bringing more than 500 people together for two days of organizing, strategizing, and celebrating. The weekend kicked off with a comedy show featuring **Margaret Cho** and **Mehran Khodabandeh** , with WFP Democratic nominees **Brad Lander (NY-10), Connie Chan (CA-11), Randy Villegas (CA-22), and Jane Kim (California Insurance Commissioner)** joining the festivities. Even **Lobo, our WFP wolf mascot** , showed up. (He’s very busy.) [](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqvlwhslwHzsYo7bshL1ic1bkV4PRhnH7RZF3DENncgqjw6v_TQFaag0JmD_5KPzWonbDX6yT5VX2uklQBZCeDqvmlOKunzR9PcG97IsaIb-z5Kzl8Wx1tibpKNnKV18HxCOOVnKtaC9pQ6eFz6ky3lt3DiaBnjB-quuTlgZlEkNMkHcn1XXj5dvauWMWKDKqEhnJvejYkxAlfAfDeesV1M8weogEZaxdJGQ-cgqxd8_SvGL-lhTdb1MXnf2noJVBGrib6zWGTAy9OIESn5x8azmjHRThNcfRg-Peaxr25aL765kqaFnui26JdhXy71i1YdDwBeGpQYOfNXBRCWULjei/4th/QuDbqUKjRRyRQRpc1Mng-A/h7/h001.4wxWxm9oEpCuiHDbRz56FiSfd-lMAooMFVbHJVrVMKU)Meanwhile, **Colorado WFP held its first-ever state convention** , bringing more than 200 people together with Democratic nominees **Melat Kiros (CO-1), Amanda Gonzalez (Colorado Secretary of State), Julie Gonzales (U.S. Senate)** , and other WFP leaders to learn, strategize, and build together. **Oregon WFP got in on the action too** , hosting its own nominating convention and bringing members together to keep building WFP power in the state. From California to Colorado to Oregon, we’re building the organization, relationships, and people power we’ll need for the fights ahead — **and having a little fun while we’re at it.**
* * *
**_WHAT'S COMING UP:_** [**WFP Mass Call**](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMbGj-ca0TYSsYMZBvIweYdJxZAP5xLg1YZaKIinIFmIxwneR9YUH85oX6XyKoEwATL_hbR3LKU0fNB3u-IwAuIx4bOHBd9r5K7vNkRhEcaWFq2Si5Xh-TKtOYHJctkU5bKpCCldo4Mg2p6Lt7qhMcE9-PVoIh-ph8-O9yUDw6p7qtInKH7jEwVKFgznoLzqr-MzWHDmA6MuBLIYkH0rP14rUE_JHU-0euCX1KvEFYSPsyHxaTePWwube4j4LNYBogg/4th/QuDbqUKjRRyRQRpc1Mng-A/h8/h001.0AsroS9dg4FWcOhCTbxYIDGq8ATvSYXNRIN9GTOTGRU) Join WFP members from across the country on **Wednesday, September 16 at 8 PM ET/5 PM PT** for our next **WFP Mass Call**. We’ll break down what’s happening in this political moment, what it means for working people, and how we organize together to build a government for the many, not the few. **[RSVP: WFP Mass Call »](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMbGj-ca0TYSsYMZBvIweYdJxZAP5xLg1YZaKIinIFmIxwneR9YUH85oX6XyKoEwATL_hbR3LKU0fNB3u-IwAuIx4bOHBd9r5K7vNkRhEcaWFceFEaHZMzqqK38UP3YYnUzCVQngv3c9E3muwRdvMXD64RfCH4PGiW2lGTBicg2mybHZ7CKwJO8N55xJ4m0axgW7DpbsVmVj7cs_N42mwjcq5Ee12oyQ6jz_TRDZGDMSscbHhWKWw0eH2QZV7jhtJnw/4th/QuDbqUKjRRyRQRpc1Mng-A/h9/h001.e-79egXpRQC7r0jOMnvxN9tPvVbSCVeLzp6iao7BksY)** Can’t make the call?**There are plenty of other ways to get involved.** [**Check out WFP events happening online and near you, and join us to organize, take action, and build power with working people across the country.**](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMbGj-ca0TYSsYMZBvIweYdJdMRKpuhAT1OnS47U4pbhVX2jLfR2-d7ssnVaByRbX5zRnfKezNOnD2FHuY7mGuv9W4oa9ms-lf1BIGARWxVWlIbH7CVEIcVXbiTXmTseuCUvbEAam17ZDbR00XTG2qmnS3BwLgBqV9c1ZB4dz_6m8nsMOMnUIp9OXfWhxUQ-J-LrAOXuJ8QiRAGPXdmvreYeFwvJ6icKOokvsuv_VQj5w/4th/QuDbqUKjRRyRQRpc1Mng-A/h10/h001.DCD6qaJswt2BaLf5TJU_aJcJOtijSqlebFJ-GwNjFAE) **[Find an event near you »](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMbGj-ca0TYSsYMZBvIweYdJdMRKpuhAT1OnS47U4pbhVX2jLfR2-d7ssnVaByRbX5zRnfKezNOnD2FHuY7mGuv-sbYqEEQbhno5iB9CXAT3IuKHuE4_0GBXTg6_6gHbOCSmSQ-fLfJQq-Fv9uy0amV2Ulx3gtT6vK9xv63cczYRmmdouhAd8449yeIc9YDdm01KDwwDqU1AVp8vSyKUjr-Q_zSv7LBGGst4U1ze5iI_3/4th/QuDbqUKjRRyRQRpc1Mng-A/h11/h001.QbBLrjWMe6thSS-D60IEIBKpG1MXoFeMP2RZgdQy5SE)**
* * *

clean_body: | | | Welcome back to the WFP newsletter, Peter! We’ve got a lot to celebrate this month. WFP champions are winning big from Michigan to Florida, our state parties are growing, and working people are showing once again that no amount of billionaire money can substitute for a movement of people who are organized and ready to fight for each other. Of course, the billionaires seem determined to test that theory. They’re pouring millions into races across the country to stop our candidates and protect the status quo (which means we must be doing something right). So, let’s get into what WFP members have been up to this month — the wins, the fights, and everything we’re building together. WFP SWEEP IN MICHIGAN Our winning streak continued in Michigan this month, where our brand-new WFP chapter celebrated a** cleansweep of our federal candidates. ** Public health expert Abdul El-Sayed won his primary for U.S. Senate, Sunrise Movement co-founder and WFP member Will Lawrence won in the 7th Congressional District, and WFP State Rep. Donavan McKinney won in the 13th District. All three ran on a bold agenda of guaranteed health care and child care, good union jobs, and taking on the corporations and AI oligarchs exploiting our communities. And the billionaire class certainly tried to stop them. Abdul faced more outside spending than** anyother Senate primary candidate in U.S. history — and won anyway. Turns out money can buy a lot of ads, but it can’t always buy an election. The wins also continued locally, with Chris Gilmer-Hill unseating a State House incumbent backed by utility money, Abbas Alawieh winning an open State Senate primary with a multiracial economic populist coalition, and Yousef Rabhi winning his primary for Ann Arbor Mayor on an economic justice platform. Michigan is part of a growing wave of WFP victories across the country, as working people prove that organized people can beat organized money. ANGIE NIXON PROVES THEM WRONG IN FLORIDA From Michigan, our winning streak headed south — where WFP champion Angie Nixon scored a major victory in Florida. Angie won her primary for U.S. Senate with more than 700,000 votes , despite being dramatically outspent by her opponent. A WFP member, labor organizer, community advocate, small-business owner, state lawmaker, and mother, Angie ran a campaign rooted in the Working Families Guarantee : health care you can count on, housing you can afford, child care when you need it, good jobs with livable wages, and a government that answers to everyday people — not billionaire bosses. The political establishment may have thought a working-class candidate like Angie couldn’t win. Florida voters had other ideas. Her decisive victory showed what we’ve long known: the South is hungry for change, and when we invest in working-class champions who speak directly to what people need, we can win. Now comes the bigger fight. Angie is headed to the general election, and the corporate interests lining up against her will have plenty more money to spend. PEOPLE POWER > NEW MAPS IN TENNESSEE Florida wasn’t the only place in the South where working people made their voices heard this month. In Tennessee, WFP champion Justin J. Pearson won the Democratic primary in the newly redrawn 9th Congressional District — on the 61st anniversary of the signing of the Voting Rights Act. timing couldn’t have been more fitting. Republicans drastically redrew Tennessee’s last majority-Black congressional district, turning a compact Memphis-based seat into a sprawling, Republican-leaning district stretching roughly 200 miles. But Justin — one of the Tennessee Three , who was expelled from the State House after protesting for gun safety — knows a thing or two about what happens when politicians try to silence the people. He defeated a State Senator backed by the local Democratic establishment and will now face a Trump-endorsed Republican this November. Republicans may have drawn themselves a new map. Now, we’re organizing to make sure working people have the final say. A HISTORIC WIN IN CALIFRONIA California officially joined this month’s win column, with a historic victory of its own, Peter. WFP-backed State Senator Aisha Wahab won the special election in California’s 14th Congressional District, making history as the first Afghan American elected to Congress. Aisha has taken on Wall Street landlords and corporate utilities and fought for affordable housing, workers, and working families — a record that drew millions**in outside spending from AIPAC-linked groups determined to stop her. But even after all that spending, Aisha came out on top. She’ll serve through January 2027, completing the remainder of Eric Swalwell’s term. But this fight is far from over: Aisha will face her opponent again this November, this time for a full two-year term in Congress. And the same forces that tried to stop her this time aren’t going anywhere. But neither are we. THE WINNING STREAK CONTINUES The summer winning streak made a stop in Arizona, too, where WFP’s bloc in the state legislature is poised to grow after Democratic primary victories from Lisbeth Arescurenaga, Miranda Lopez, and Alberto Flores. And Arizona wasn’t alone: in Connecticut, Maryam Khan, Jack Fazzino, Moise Carelus, Toni Lombardi, and Angie Parkinson pulled off a clean sweep of their state legislative primaries, while across the country in Washington State, Jaelynn Scott and Kelabe Tewolde won their state legislative primaries and longtime organizer Nilu Jenks won her primary for Seattle City Council District 5. But we’re not done yet, Peter! Massachusetts heads to the polls on September 1st , where WFP has endorsed a slate of eight working-class champions for the state legislature: Latoya Gayle, Carey McDonald, Daniel Lander, Lorena Betts, John Drinkwater, Tara Hong, Johnnie McKnight, and Celina Reyes. They’re union members, educators, organizers, and local leaders running to take on business as usual on Beacon Hill and put working families first. ELON MUSK VS. WFP Apparently, WFP has gotten under the skin of the world’s richest man. Last year, Delaware legislators passed the controversial “Billionaire’s Bill,” handing massive giveaways to Elon Musk — who was apparently in desperate need of another $56 billion — and other ultra-wealthy corporate shareholders. Now, WFP is backing a slate of working families champions challenging legislators who supported the bill, and Musk’s corporate allies are fighting back. Corporate law firms and their allies are pouring more than $1 million through super PACs and nonprofits into Delaware legislative races to protect incumbents who backed the Billionaire’s Bill. One donor is even the same firm Musk and Tesla used while the legislation was under consideration. That’s an extraordinary amount of money for these races — and a pretty good indication that our challenges have them nervous. This is exactly the kind of corporate power WFP is organizing to take on. If billionaires and their lawyers want to spend a fortune trying to stop us, they’re welcome to try. BUILDING THE PARTY Taking on billionaire power requires building some serious people power of our own — and that’s exactly what WFP members have been doing across the country. California WFP recently held its , bringing more than 500 people together for two days of organizing, strategizing, and celebrating. The weekend kicked off with a comedy show featuring Margaret Cho and Mehran Khodabandeh , with WFP Democratic nominees Brad Lander (NY-10), Connie Chan (CA-11), Randy Villegas (CA-22), and Jane Kim (California Insurance Commissioner) joining the festivities. Even Lobo, our WFP wolf mascot , showed up. (He’s very busy.) , Colorado WFP held its first-ever state convention , bringing more than 200 people together with Democratic nominees Melat Kiros (CO-1), Amanda Gonzalez (Colorado Secretary of State), Julie Gonzales (U.S. Senate) , and other WFP leaders to learn, strategize, and build together. Oregon WFP got in on the action too , hosting its own nominating convention and bringing members together to keep building WFP power in the state. From California to Colorado to Oregon, we’re building the organization, relationships, and people power we’ll need for the fights ahead — and having a little fun while we’re at it. WHAT'S COMING UP: Join WFP members from across the country on Wednesday, September 16 at 8 PM ET/5 PM PT for our next WFP Mass Call. We’ll break down what’s happening in this political moment, what it means for working people, and how we organize together to build a government for the many, not the few. Can’t make the call?There are plenty of other ways to get involved. That’s a wrap for this month, Peter! From some pretty spectacular primary victories to building our party state by state, WFP members are proving what’s possible when working people organize together — and we’re not done yet. We have big fights ahead of us this fall. Our candidates are going up against billionaire-funded super PACs, corporate interests, and Republicans who will spend whatever it takes to keep working people out of power. name: Clay Middleton
subject: Our Issues are Too Blue for this District To Be Red
body:
Help break South Carolina’s Supermajority in November
Hey Peter,
**It’s Clay Middleton, the Democratic Nominee for SC House District 116.** As a husband, father, and resident of South Carolina, everything that we need to live, from groceries and gas to health care, is becoming more expensive, and our wages haven’t kept up.
Our issues are too blue for red leadership, and too many people are ignored by the politicians who represent them. **[Will you split a donation between Wes Moore and our campaign to ensure that everyone gets their needs met?](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260825-2.mViKjC&refcode=em-20260825-2&t=1&akid=1820%2E1086043%2E6vqkb5)**
**[Split $25 now!](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/1438?c0=wes-em-20260825-2.vF-J02&refcode=em-20260825-2&t=2&akid=1820%2E1086043%2E6vqkb5)**
Many people have left the area because they can’t afford to live here, hollowing out our sense of community. I’m running to deliver practical solutions on affordability so our neighbors can stay and thrive here. This struggle isn’t just in this community, but exists throughout the US.
**We won the June 9th primary with 67.48% of the vote, because voters want someone who is dedicated to putting their needs first.** But the primary is just the beginning; I’ll need your help to keep the momentum going to help break the Republican supermajority in November.
**When elected, I will fight for healthcare, housing, and opportunities for all residents, and electing me in November will help break the supermajority in the South Carolina House.** That means the ability to push back against greedy companies, banning books, restricting a woman's right to make her own decisions, more data centers, fewer voting rights, and protecting our way of life.
With this seat, I can make the South Carolina General Assembly focus on the issues that connect us all.
I’m committed to this district and the country, and I will use my experience and relationships to solve problems and create opportunities. **[If you think we need more servant leaders, will you consider splitting a donation between Wes Moore and our campaign? Every dollar helps us win back this flippable district and elect those who’ll put people first.](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260825-2.mViKjC&refcode=em-20260825-2&t=3&akid=1820%2E1086043%2E6vqkb5)**
In service,
Clay Middleton
Shaping 116 Together

Fellow Patriot - Six weeks ago, Governor Henry McMaster appointed me to the United States Senate.

Since then, I've gone to work, serving the people of South Carolina, from being the lead sponsor on the Russian Sanctions bill, to casting the deciding vote to confirm President Trump's Attorney General, Todd Blanche.

If we got this much done in just six weeks, imagine what we can accomplish together in six years!

Today is it - the runoff Election is finally here. **[I cannot do this without you._I need your help, Fellow Patriot_.](http://links.ourdefenseofamerica.com/u/click?_t=aa3ef0db03454a26b650c9ca7e919386&_m=00fb16d01e2f4042b24fa778a9033e1a&_e=EPz56WI7qMXUVkkd4kIADpdEb438SI_AP7_xHarUs9J3Eja99RHw5ioHHEcvBluv1fe99vkVNkFYCUgX3pnejh8nFk6XAAJAU4tsdy5epZfzcErMnP53a9KNycGUn0V7fMnF6nFWDsc3R6FuSQ5vXhY3tdPeZHBMHFfA5pp_QDX3p6EZ6yxzs5sEyUnFBPGw9S8urswa2_B7BZHwW1rE91mCz_ryzAt8LNknuTzJwVlVWerPkRyMGwJvrZgtjaJVGdZpp2Ypw1qisJGg_Yik8ZYs76HFCPVpf10OfWKT6KBcj-t9dJlrk-UziMovDUOtNuNyhspRsKYXyjDEYujYHqK7BTZGKMqaSV4xbQI56xEIsNXfMSK9ZH0wHhVg30hvHP8yQPijcavms6UAfcBZj7djSqEZGIRy6HduUHpHrA8jbW0p7wr_LIta4iu9ep_Pecq8r8JrCwgy2ZMYMFnnwJkyk1B_3Zyh_0eyyZ1rELNtV8-s2MVC6hiD8NVUoIu9zNb7IfLfIfRDg3n3n5vcR7Kr83ySnT0vIo5f4NjWQ9koxUfV6Ste88_grsYVFEgf7wlqBrj-cWDPWZveFKeMGfIJ0z4FfWpkImyMTo0K7EqE7pkGe86KidhgeVQXxxbTiwk21FXKiXyNSUmLqyGS1Oc4-CXiwhpYgNNcZxuj9q7NiXLSUOibZ_SPmIWdxIeWm1fAamruFvRjv5KoWU-ruIWkV91YG7a27GWAphVM78aAQ4rTVNqincoMkuzxPPvY)**

Help me reach every voter - and fuel the fight still ahead - before midnight. | Fellow Patriot - Six weeks ago, Governor Henry McMaster appointed me to the United States Senate. Since then, I've gone to work, serving the people of South Carolina, from being the lead sponsor on the Russian Sanctions bill, to casting the deciding vote to confirm President Trump's Attorney General, Todd Blanche. If we got this much done in just six weeks, imagine what we can accomplish together in six years! Today is it - the runoff Election is finally here. I'm not a politician. I never expected to be running for office, and I never wanted to. I'm doing this because I'm answering President Trump's call to serve, and because I believe South Carolina deserves a fighter in the Senate. Like Lindsey, I grew up in the back of a bar and liquor store, in one room. My parents worked every single day to make ends meet. There was no time for sickness and few vacations, because if the doors weren't open, no money was coming in. That's the kind of work ethic I've carried my whole life, from running a state agency with 130 employees and a $90 million budget to turning it into a national model for helping people find work and live independently. I'm a mother, a grandmother, and a wife. And today, I'm asking you to help me win and finish this so we can look to November. | Peter,
You know, every now and then, my team tries to tell me how to play the game... how to be a "good politician".
But let me tell you, I'm not in this to play games or be a career politician. I'm in this to fight for what I believe in and to make a real difference.
I'm tired of the politicians who promise one thing and then do another. Who say whatever it takes to get elected, and then forget about the people who put them there.

#### _**[The future of the Democratic Party won't be decided by cable news panels--it'll be built in our communities, our schools, and conversations like this one. We started Endless Urgency to get beyond the daily outrage and talk honestly about the politics--and the real life--that shapes how we show up for each other. If you believe in building that kind of community, becoming a paid subscriber helps support our small, dedicated team and keeps this work growing every single day.](https://substack.com/redirect/d1501812-01af-4683-a5cd-99cb84a1efea?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**_

* * *
Hey folks,
[Katie Phang](https://open.substack.com/users/21818709-katie-phang?utm_source=mentions) and I are back for another episode of _Breaking Bread_. We started with back-to-school and the emotional reality of watching our kids grow up, then found our way into community, the current political moment we are in as we approach the midterms, and what it actually means to show up right now. That's the thing about these conversations--we never quite know where they're going, and that's kind of the point.
* [**00:09:10**] Back-to-school hits me harder than expected as I talk about my son starting second grade--and how fast this whole parenting thing moves.
* [**00:17:21**] Katie shares the advice she gave her daughter about starting over: be yourself, find your people, and trust that your people will find you.
* [**00:25:30**] We dig into the races people may be overlooking--and why state and local elections matter just as much as the national fights consuming our feeds.
* [**00:30:00**] I share some big personal news: I'm taking on a new local role in Chicago and putting more of my energy into organizing, mutual aid, and building community right here at home.
* [**00:38:00**] The conversation comes full circle: resistance doesn't always mean marching in the streets. Sometimes it's helping your neighbors. Sometimes it's being a good parent. Sometimes it's taking the damn nap.

This conversation is really about how we keep going without losing ourselves. Parenting. Politics. Friendship. Community. Showing up where you can, with whatever you have to give. If you're exhausted by the national chaos but still looking for a way to matter, this one is for you. **If you value honest conversations like this, help me keep them going.**

With urgency,
--Mike

The American public health system is undergoing its most dramatic restructuring in a generation. Under the Trump administration, new leadership at the National Institutes of Health (NIH) and Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) is implementing far-reaching reforms while simultaneous criminal accountability efforts target former pandemic officials. The convergence of institutional overhaul, legal investigations, and continued investment in next-generation vaccine technology has created a volatile landscape that critics describe as a long-overdue reckoning with institutional abuse of power.
**NIH Reforms Under Dr. Jay Bhattacharya**
President Trump's NIH Director, Dr. Jay Bhattacharya, has moved swiftly to implement an ambitious reform agenda. A Stanford physician who rose to prominence during COVID-19 as a vocal critic of extended lockdowns, Bhattacharya is reshaping the nation's premier health research agency from the ground up.
Central to Bhattacharya's agenda is the development of an entirely new pandemic playbook. Working with fellow NIH officials, he has argued that the world needs fundamentally different preparedness strategies--ones that reject what the administration characterizes as the medically authoritarian approaches of the previous era, including prolonged school closures, economy-wide shutdowns, and top-down mandates. The proposed framework emphasizes targeted protection, individual medical autonomy, and evidence-based decision-making that accounts for collateral public health damages.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f4465657-62b6-4cfd-b6b1-babaee48ae5e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Perhaps the most concrete policy shift is the complete termination of federal funding for dangerous gain-of-function (dGOF) research. In August 2026, the NIH released a comprehensive government-wide policy banning such high-risk life sciences research, which involves genetically modifying pathogens to study their transmissibility and virulence. Bhattacharya described this as a "paradigm shift in federal oversight," introducing enhanced review requirements, independent assessments, and strong enforcement mechanisms to prevent risky pathogen manipulation. The ban addresses long-standing Republican concerns that such research may have contributed to the origins of COVID-19.
Bhattacharya has also pledged to address the beleaguered Countermeasures Injury Compensation Program (CICP), which handles claims from individuals injured by COVID-19 countermeasures, including vaccines. Congressional committees have warned that without major reforms, the CICP backlog could take a decade to resolve, with thousands of claimants waiting years for decisions. The administration has signaled support for establishing a more transparent vaccine injury review body to restore public trust in vaccination programs.
Institutionally, Bhattacharya has consolidated authority by also serving as acting CDC director while the administration searched for a permanent appointee--a dual role that has drawn both praise for enabling unified decision-making and criticism for concentrating too much power in one official.
**New CDC Leadership: Dr. Erica Schwartz**
The search for permanent CDC leadership concluded in August 2026 when the Senate confirmed Dr. Erica Schwartz as the agency's new director by a narrow 51-44 vote. Schwartz, a 54-year-old retired rear admiral, became the first Black woman to lead the CDC and the 22nd leader of the Atlanta-based agency.
During her confirmation hearings before the Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee on July 15, 2026, Schwartz presented herself as a defender of scientific integrity within an administration whose health policies have frequently generated controversy. "Public health is in my DNA," she testified. "If confirmed, my first priority will be restoring trust in public health institutions through radical transparency and unwavering scientific integrity."
Schwartz's most widely circulated testimony came when she declared: "As CDC director, my sacred responsibility is to provide the American people with public health guidance that is clear, honest, and evidence-based. I will never betray the science."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/083f8670-9eaa-43fb-a258-fc0469196034?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The confirmation has split the administration's coalition. President Trump praised her military background and leadership credentials, while some "Make America Healthy Again" (MAHA) activists have expressed skepticism due to her institutional ties and support for childhood vaccines. Reports indicate she also backed some actions by HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., suggesting she may navigate a delicate path between institutional continuity and the administration's reform agenda.
Senators pressing for stability at the agencies noted that confirming Schwartz and other nominees would be tasked with "bringing stability and restoring public trust in HHS." Schwartz has also emphasized modernizing the CDC into a "near real-time public health enterprise capable of detecting threats early and responding faster," while pledging to empower state, local, and tribal health authorities as the operational backbone of American public health.
**Criminal Accountability Campaigns**
These administrative reforms have developed alongside an unprecedented push for criminal accountability targeting former pandemic leaders. A nationwide campaign organized through advocacy networks has filed criminal referral requests with the attorneys general of all 50 states, urging investigations and prosecutions of Dr. Anthony Fauci and other senior public-health officials for alleged roles in what the campaign describes as the "COVID Criminal Enterprise."
The referrals allege a pattern of misconduct during the pandemic, including suppression of alternative viewpoints, dissemination of misleading public health guidance, and potential perjury before Congress regarding the origins of COVID-19 and NIH funding decisions related to gain-of-function research.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b912517c-17a2-4213-aa89-da6c177883f9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The campaign gained momentum following Fauci's appearance before the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee on July 29, 2026, where he invoked his Fifth Amendment right against self-incrimination rather than answer questions about his role in pandemic policymaking. On August 6, 2026, the committee voted 8-5 along party lines to hold Fauci in contempt of Congress, clearing the way for a criminal referral to the Department of Justice. Senator Rand Paul, who has long accused Fauci of lying about NIH-funded research and the lab-leak hypothesis, has been the driving force behind the contempt effort.
President Trump subsequently stated he is open to DOJ prosecution of Fauci, saying "maybe he should" face criminal charges. Legal analysts note that while President Biden had previously pardoned Fauci in the final days of his administration, that pardon does not extend to state-level charges or to conduct and testimony occurring after the pardon was issued.
Meanwhile, two NIH scientists recently faced charges related to virus samples, though colleagues characterized the case as largely about paperwork violations rather than malfeasance.
**Next-Generation Vaccine Technology**
Despite the NIH's retreat from supporting certain mRNA programs and Bhattacharya's criticism of pandemic-era vaccine policies, major funding for next-generation genetic vaccine technology continues through private philanthropy. The Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation has been investing heavily in self-replicating RNA (srRNA) and self-amplifying mRNA vaccine platforms, which could produce equivalent immune responses at substantially lower doses than conventional mRNA vaccines.
San Diego-based Replicate Bioscience has received multiple Gates Foundation grants totaling approximately $10 million to develop srRNA vaccines for tuberculosis, malaria, and HIV using the company's novel platform. Self-amplifying mRNA vaccines encode both the target antigen and a viral replicase that amplifies the RNA inside cells, potentially allowing smaller doses and broader global distribution. However, the technology raises fresh biosafety questions, particularly given the administration's new restrictions on gain-of-function and risky life sciences research.
A Phase 3 trial of Arcturus Therapeutics' self-amplifying COVID-19 mRNA vaccine published in March 2026 reported longitudinally enhanced antibody function, suggesting the platform may have durability advantages over earlier vaccines. Whether such technologies will face heightened scrutiny under Bhattacharya's risk-based framework remains an open question.
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved mFlusiva, the first-ever messenger RNA (mRNA) flu vaccine, manufactured by Moderna.
**Whistleblowers and Allegations of Suppression**
Throughout the pandemic, physicians challenging official narratives faced significant institutional pushback. Dr. Pierre Kory, a critical care physician and president of the Front Line COVID-19 Critical Care Alliance (FLCCC), testified multiple times before Congress about early outpatient treatment protocols and alleged suppression of alternative therapies. While his advocacy for ivermectin was widely disputed in the medical establishment, Kory and colleagues argued that government agencies ignored or actively suppressed potentially effective treatments while rushing to approve novel vaccines under emergency use authorizations.
These whistleblower allegations have fueled the broader narrative that pandemic decision-making was characterized by groupthink, censorship of dissent, and harmful consequences for ordinary Americans--including educational deficits from school closures, economic devastation, and vaccine injuries left uncompensated.
The American public health system in 2026 finds itself at a crossroads. Bhattacharya's NIH reforms, Schwartz's pledges of scientific integrity, criminal referral campaigns, and continued advancement of genetic vaccine technology represent overlapping and sometimes contradictory forces. The administration's supporters argue that these changes constitute necessary accountability after years of what they characterize as a chilling abuse of power--an era of mandates, censorship, and scientific opacity that eroded public trust. Critics counter that politicized prosecutions and rapid institutional overhauls risk destabilizing the nation's capacity to respond to future health threats.
What is clear is that the pandemic era's shadow continues to loom over every policy decision, every confirmation hearing, and every funding announcement. Whether the reforms will genuinely restore public confidence--or merely replace one set of partisan governance with another--remains the defining question for American public health.

Early in the pandemic, we passed a policy to send funding to states and local governments responding to unhoused people’s needs.

Landlords’ refusal to rent to individuals with a criminal record impacts 1 in 3 adults in this country.
Ayanna’s family has been impacted by mass incarceration, so she knows how urgently we must change our criminal legal system.
I’ve been proud to support her policies to **guarantee the right to vote** for citizens with criminal records, **end corporate profiteering in incarceration,** and move federal policy toward **community-based solutions**.

I wanted to take a moment to give you a quick, honest update on where things stand in MI-04.

[ ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137917337/642363362/510768709?refcode=email-header&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTIzMCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyOGNjZjg3ZC1jOWEwLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlmMWQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=g7NEnLSnoNpEm2dlSMc-ijwu7uVWZletwxoB_VlnAKE=) Hi there, it’s Simone, Sean’s campaign manager. I wanted to take a moment to give you a quick, honest update on where things stand in MI-04. August has been a non-stop month here in Southwest Michigan, and a lot has changed in our race. **So if you’re just tuning in now or need a quick refresher on where things stand, here’s what’s happening:**
* **Sean officially won the Democratic nomination for MI-04!** Thanks to supporters like you, our team powered through the primary with incredible momentum.

* **Nate Silver named our race a TOSS-UP, and _Split Ticket_ predicted our race will come down to less than a 1% margin.** The nation is watching this district, and experts agree that MI-04 is one of the top flip opportunities in the country.

* **The national GOP is terrified.** The House GOP super PAC just launched a staggering $22 MILLION in attacks across vulnerable districts — explicitly targeting races like ours right here in MI-04.

Rob Bonta tried to bury the truth — The fight for election integrity continues

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/N_4ME4HbXvp?e=1facf02470&c2id=205919520b3860dafbe9b9f5dda2019d)

Friend,
I have one simple question:
**Why is Bonta preventing me from exposing possible election fraud?**
Evidence of possible voter fraud in the Prop 50 election landed on my desk.
I did my job — got a legal warrant signed by a judge so we could simply count the ballots.
That’s it. Count them.Then AG Rob Bonta ordered me to stop. **I refused**.
---
| | | | | [Must Watch](https://us.list-manage.com/mJxjVIkpsdS?e=1facf02470&c2id=205919520b3860dafbe9b9f5dda2019d)
---
| |
No Attorney General in 250 years has the power to shut down a lawful investigation just because he says so.
He lost in Superior Court.He lost in the Appellate Court.
Now he’s at the highest court **demanding something never argued before** : the power to kill any investigation he wants — into his friends, donors, or allies.
**His lawyers still can’t explain the 45,000-vote discrepancy.** They just say “it doesn’t exist” and claim _the Sheriff found no evidence of fraud._
Of course we didn’t. Bonta stopped the investigation before we could finish.
So I’ll ask you:
**Why not just let us count the ballots?****What is Rob Bonta so afraid of?**
This is pure lawfare against me for looking under a rock I clearly wasn’t supposed to look under.
I’ll keep fighting.**Will you stand with me?**
— Sheriff Chad Bianco

body:
# [](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/43706?t=1&akid=241034%2E444211%2Eew-sQR)
Yesterday was a hot day at UTA as we officially kicked off our Every Campus Counts Tour!
But students, PXP volunteers and organizers were up for it. Lots of great conversations as we met, registered and made plans to stay in touch with every young voter we came across.
A few stories that stood out to me include: Corey, majoring in biology and history on his way to becoming a teacher in Texas public schools. He told me that he and his wife (a surgical tech in a local hospital) want to have kids, but not sure that they can do it in Texas. Explained to me that they are lifelong Christians, members of their church, but think the abortion ban could put them in harm’s way as they attempt to start a family.
Giovanni is in the aerospace engineering grad program, wants to go to NASA next. Benefitted from a program at UTA that helps young Texans who otherwise wouldn’t have a chance.
Met a young man whose parents immigrated from Liberia, now getting registered and voting to make sure that he’s a voice for his parents.
Latricia told me that she makes sure to vote in every election because of what happened in the school board elections in Mansfield — every vote counts! she says.
Marc became a citizen on Friday and we registered him to vote yesterday!
Tina told me she’s studying public health so that “those who are underrepresented can be represented the ways that corporations and big insurance companies are.”
Keno stopped by to check his registration and said he gives back by putting on punk rock shows to raise awareness and money for those impacted by ICE raids.
Was there when Alexander and Spruha got registered, big smiles.
Ethan told me, “I’m not really a Democrat or Republican. If anything, I identify with Teddy Roosevelt’s Bull Moose Party.” He explained that he grew up in rural Texas, his family running cattle. Land is important, conservation is important, fighting the concentration of power is important.
Elizabeth knocked it out of the park first time volunteering and so did the experienced Russ, on fire on a hot day. Props to Emmanuel and student PXP chapter.
And Grace got registered by Jay!
[**I’m traveling to college campuses through Election Day because this is the work that works. Can you help me stay on the road by pitching in any amount today?**](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=pbp-em-20260825.3Z-KAm&refcode=ema20260825-241034&t=3&akid=241034%2E444211%2Eew-sQR)
Thank you,
Beto

Latricia told me that she makes sure to vote in every election because of what happened in the school board elections in Mansfield — every vote counts! she says. Marc became a citizen on Friday and we registered him to vote yesterday! Tina told me she’s studying public health so that “those who are underrepresented can be represented the ways that corporations and big insurance companies are.” Keno stopped by to check his registration and said he gives back by putting on punk rock shows to raise awareness and money for those impacted by ICE raids. Was there when Alexander and Spruha got registered, big smiles. Ethan told me, “I’m not really a Democrat or Republican. If anything, I identify with Teddy Roosevelt’s Bull Moose Party.” He explained that he grew up in rural Texas, his family running cattle. Land is important, conservation is important, fighting the concentration of power is important. Elizabeth knocked it out of the park first time volunteering and so did the experienced Russ, on fire on a hot day. Props to Emmanuel and student PXP chapter. And Grace got registered by Jay! Thank you, Beto

My mom is all in, friend, ready to fight on our behalf and move our great state toward progress. | | | I need you to hear what the man in charge of your mail just did — and what happened after.
A federal judge issued an order barring Postmaster General David Steiner — by name — from finalizing a rule that restricts mail ballots. He finalized it anyway. Quietly, at night, timed to take effect before the public could even see it.
**Let's walk through this beat-by-beat:**
Back in June, Steiner sat before the Senate and promised, under oath, that USPS "would comply with any court orders regarding voting by mail." Not a casual remark — a commitment, made to the committee responsible for overseeing his agency.
Then a federal judge told him, by name, to stop. Ten days later, he finished the rule anyway.
Now here's the update, and it's not good. **Yesterday, the Supreme Court's conservative majority handed Trump an interim win** — pausing a separate ruling that had blocked his mail voting order in 23 states. They didn't rule the order legal. They just said those states waited too long to sue, even though, as _**Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson wrote in dissent, the Court "needlessly injects chaos and uncertainty into the upcoming midterm elections"**_ and never explains when states were supposed to act.
Before we go any further: Will you chip in $25 or $50 to Equal Opportunity Now right now to help us keep fighting this?
Here's the one piece of good news: USPS itself is still blocked, nationwide, from implementing Steiner's rule — that's the separate order he already defied once. The legal fight is not over.
I demanded Steiner resign. I told him plainly: A Postmaster General who promises Congress he'll follow court orders, then does the exact opposite, has forfeited the trust required to run an agency responsible for delivering the ballots of 240 million Americans. I gave him until August 31st to respond.
If Steiner can defy a named federal court order and pay no price — and now get bailed out by the Supreme Court on top of it — every official watching learns the same lesson: The courts are optional if the President wants something badly enough.
[**We are not going to let that lesson stick. Winning these fights takes all of us doing our part.

Peter,
**A billionaire tax. Medicare for All. No more endless wars.**
That platform seems like common sense, right?
It should be, but too many of our politicians are bought and paid for by big corporations and special interests to oppose any progressive reforms.
When the wealthy and well-connected flood our elections with money, they expect to get a government rigged in their favor — while everyone else gets stuck with the bill. It’s worked like this in Washington for too long and it’s time it ends.
That’s where folks like David Hogg and his organization Leaders We Deserve come in. Every day, they are backing young progressive candidates across the country who aren’t afraid to run on a bold platform to move our country forward.
Leaders We Deserve is electing candidates who buck expectations and defy the odds, both winning longshot battles and moving the needle in competitive races. And the leaders they’re electing are already making real change. Just look at New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, who Leaders helped elect earlier this year.
We can win these fights and so many more if we unrig Washington and break big money’s grip on our politics. But that only happens when grassroots supporters like you step up and claim a part of this movement. It takes _all of us_ doing our part.
**[Will you chip in $5 or whatever you can to Leaders We Deserve and my campaign today? Your support will help us build the future we all want to see.](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260825_1_khanna.-0Lm50&refcode=em20260825-3919&amount=5&t=3&akid=3919%2E587540%2ExYog4C)**

Onward,
Ro Khanna

Meet Coach Tuberville:

**Coach Tuberville was born in Camden, Arkansas, the third of three children of Olive and Charles Tuberville. College Football 's 2004 Coach of the Year and two-time SEC Coach of the Year, Tommy Tuberville is most often recognized for his success on the field. But it is the legacy of his father, a highly decorated WWII veteran and Purple Heart recipient, that motivates Coach Tuberville to give back to the brave men and women of the United States Armed Forces.

In 1989 Coach Tuberville met his future wife, Suzanne Fette, at the Sugar Bowl in New Orleans. They were married in 1991 and have two boys, Tucker and Troy, who continue to make their dad proud.

In his career as a College Football Coach, Tommy started a long and successful career at the University of Miami, starting as a graduate assistant and rising to the Hurricanes' defensive coordinator. He led the Canes to three AP national championships and coached future Hall of Famers Ray Lewis and Warren Sapp, as well as Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson.

In 1998, Coach Tuberville was announced as the next head coach for the Auburn Tigers. Tuberville's time at Auburn was a success by any measure, as the Tigers captured eight consecutive bowl appearances, including five New Year's Day bowl appearances, five SEC Western Division titles, one SEC Championship, and a 13-0 season in 2004, after which Coach Tuberville was once again named the AP's SEC Coach of the Year. For his efforts during the perfect 2004 season, Tuberville would be named Paul "Bear" Bryant Coach of the Year, Associated Press Coach of the Year, Walter Camp Coach of the Year, Sporting News Coach of the Year, and AFCA Coach of the Year, among others.

I want to update you on a tragedy in New Mexico that deserves our attention and demands answers. **On May 13, a medical aircraft carrying two pilots and two flight nurses left Roswell for Ruidoso to pick up a patient, but the plane never arrived.** All four crew members tragically lost their lives when the aircraft crashed in the Capitan Mountains. The crash also sparked a wildfire that burned for three weeks, destroying more than 30,000 acres, forcing evacuations, and requiring more than 1,000 personnel to fight it. The National Transportation Safety Board’s report on the crash has raised incredibly serious questions about whether military GPS jamming in the area contributed to the crash. **We need to know exactly what happened.** I joined New Mexico’s congressional delegation in demanding that the Department of Defense fully cooperate with investigators, work with aviation officials to prevent another tragedy, and answer basic questions about its actions that night. We’re also asking whether the Department will take responsibility for the enormous costs borne by the victims’ families and by the federal, state, and local agencies that responded to the crash and the wildfire that followed. Four people lost their lives. Their families deserve transparency. New Mexicans deserve to know whether this could have been prevented. **And every person who gets on an airplane deserves to be sure that military activities will not put civilian flights at risk.** This is part of the responsibility I take seriously every day: protecting New Mexicans, safeguarding our communities and public lands, responding to wildfires, and holding the powerful accountable when their decisions put people at risk. As military technology and electronic warfare become more sophisticated, we have to make sure our safety systems keep pace. National security and public safety cannot be treated as competing priorities. I’ll keep pressing for answers, and I’ll keep you updated as we learn more. — Martin https://www.martinheinrich.com/

### The Killing of Mustangs and the Violence of Erasure

---

The news out of Washington this August is ugly and depressingly familiar: a New York Times investigation confirmed that the Trump administration has accelerated the sale of federally protected wild mustangs, with livestock records tracing hundreds of these horses from government corrals to slaughterhouses in Canada. Sales have exploded from 793 horses in 2024 to 2,387 in 2025. What was once a sacred covenant under the Wild Free-Roaming Horses and Burros Act has become a liquidation. The symbolism is hard to miss -- America is killing its own mythology, one auction at a time.
This real-life atrocity finds an unexpected mirror in a scene from *Yellowstone*. In Season 5, Episode 12 -- "Counting Coup" -- a wild stallion is captured and brought to the ranch. Young Carter, still learning his way around horses, finds himself trapped in a stall with the terrified animal. Colby Mayfield, the quiet, decent cowboy who has been a fixture of the ranch since Season 1, rushes in to save Carter. He succeeds, but the horse's thrashing hooves trample him to death.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/49c0480c-17a4-4852-8996-10d952911ddd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
What follows is the narrative choice that matters. There was mutterings about putting the stallion down. The easiest thing would be to destroy what hurt them -- to punish the animal for being wild. But they didn't. The horse was not killed, because the Yellowstone hands understand something elemental: the stallion was not evil. It was not guilty. It was simply wild, which is not a capital crime. They killed it in the stall. Destroying it did not resurrect Colby. It only compound the loss with further violence.
Had the ranch followed the Trump administration's apparent playbook, the stallion would be glue and dog food by dawn. But 'Yellowstone' chose to be more humane than America itself.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c0987115-f2f8-4573-a0ff-55c14acc50db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
This is where Beth Dutton enters the metaphor. For five seasons, Beth medicates her way through existence -- vodka, pills, whatever deadens the static of her trauma: the day she watched her mother die, the abortion and sterilization that followed, the silence and shame her father weaponized, getting blown up, the cruelty that became her armor. She does not process her past; she erases its sensory details. She treats her own memories the way the BLM now treats mustangs -- as inconvenient surplus to be disposed of quietly, preferably out of sight.
But erasure is not healing. It is anesthesia, not surgery.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f85963a9-68fb-4b8c-b34e-d4483c16cae0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The mustang is the American West made flesh -- unbroken, ungovernable, roaming land that technology has otherwise subdued. You cannot domesticate a continent without killing its symbols first. The Trump administration's slaughter-by-proxy achieves the same thing Beth achieves with her morning vodka: it makes the problem temporarily absent, but the root festers. You cannot drink away your trauma any more than you can sell away your heritage and pretend the blood isn't on your ledger.
The deeper parallel is about what authenticity costs and what cowardice looks like. In 'Yellowstone', sparing the stallion was harder than killing it and a ride to the train station. It required the cowboys to accept grief without vengeance. It required them to live alongside the thing that hurt them. The ranch chose that harder path. America, in the summer of 2026, is choosing the easy one -- treating national heritage as a surplus commodity, sanctioning its destruction, and winking at the paperwork while trucks rumble north.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/30157f39-9cfc-401e-a707-ba4299390003?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The most damning detail in a NY Times investigation was not the policy itself but the transaction: an inexperienced buyer -- reportedly in New Jersey -- took possession of dozens of mustangs from the Bureau of Land Management for twenty-five dollars apiece, a price so low it barely covers a halter. No adoption paperwork showed a ranch, a nonprofit, or any coherent plan for the animals. Trucks arrived the following night, and the horses vanished from the federal ledger into an undocumented pipeline with no declared use, no destination, and no plausible explanation other than the one the government pretends not to see. When you sell a living symbol for less than a parking meter fee to a buyer with no visible infrastructure or expertise, you are not rehoming wildlife; you are staging a funeral by freight.
Beth's arc warns us what happens when we keep choosing erasure. The pills don't cure; they postpone. The vodka doesn't numb; it deepens the fracture. And the mustangs, once gone, will not come back. You cannot bottle and export a symbol of freedom, only its carcass. She is the horse. Jamie is the result. The train station is the final destination.
The irony is acute. 'Yellowstone', a Paramount soap opera often dismissed as cowboys versus condos, understood in a single episode the moral mathematics this administration cannot grasp: killing the wounded does not make you whole. The stallion lives, because the story recognized that some wildness is worth preserving even when it's inconvenient, even when it hurts us, especially when it costs us something.
America, meanwhile, is busy proving it prefers the bottle -- or in this case, the abattoir. And the hangover will last generations.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a48d6abc-9244-4c01-be5a-7f5af5158d39?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

It is anesthesia, not surgery. | | ---|---|--- The mustang is the American West made flesh -- unbroken, ungovernable, roaming land that technology has otherwise subdued. You cannot domesticate a continent without killing its symbols first. The Trump administration's slaughter-by-proxy achieves the same thing Beth achieves with her morning vodka: it makes the problem temporarily absent, but the root festers. You cannot drink away your trauma any more than you can sell away your heritage and pretend the blood isn't on your ledger. The deeper parallel is about what authenticity costs and what cowardice looks like. In 'Yellowstone', sparing the stallion was harder than killing it and a ride to the train station. It required the cowboys to accept grief without vengeance. It required them to live alongside the thing that hurt them. The ranch chose that harder path. America, in the summer of 2026, is choosing the easy one -- treating national heritage as a surplus commodity, sanctioning its destruction, and winking at the paperwork while trucks rumble north. | | ---|---|--- The most damning detail in a NY Times investigation was not the policy itself but the transaction: an inexperienced buyer -- reportedly in New Jersey -- took possession of dozens of mustangs from the Bureau of Land Management for twenty-five dollars apiece, a price so low it barely covers a halter. No adoption paperwork showed a ranch, a nonprofit, or any coherent plan for the animals. Trucks arrived the following night, and the horses vanished from the federal ledger into an undocumented pipeline with no declared use, no destination, and no plausible explanation other than the one the government pretends not to see. When you sell a living symbol for less than a parking meter fee to a buyer with no visible infrastructure or expertise, you are not rehoming wildlife; you are staging a funeral by freight. Beth's arc warns us what happens when we keep choosing erasure. The pills don't cure; they postpone. The vodka doesn't numb; it deepens the fracture. And the mustangs, once gone, will not come back. You cannot bottle and export a symbol of freedom, only its carcass. She is the horse. Jamie is the result. The train station is the final destination. The irony is acute. 'Yellowstone', a Paramount soap opera often dismissed as cowboys versus condos, understood in a single episode the moral mathematics this administration cannot grasp: killing the wounded does not make you whole. The stallion lives, because the story recognized that some wildness is worth preserving even when it's inconvenient, even when it hurts us, especially when it costs us something. America, meanwhile, is busy proving it prefers the bottle -- or in this case, the abattoir. And the hangover will last generations. | | ---|---|--- ? You're currently a free subscriber to . The news out of Washington this August is ugly and depressingly familiar: a New York Times investigation confirmed that the Trump administration has accelerated the sale of federally protected wild mustangs, with livestock records tracing hundreds of these horses from government corrals to slaughterhouses in Canada. Sales have exploded from 793 horses in 2024 to 2,387 in 2025. What was once a sacred covenant under the Wild Free-Roaming Horses and Burros Act has become a liquidation. The symbolism is hard to miss -- America is killing its own mythology, one auction at a time.
This real-life atrocity finds an unexpected mirror in a scene from *Yellowstone*. In Season 5, Episode 12 -- "Counting Coup" -- a wild stallion is captured and brought to the ranch. Young Carter, still learning his way around horses, finds himself trapped in a stall with the terrified animal. Colby Mayfield, the quiet, decent cowboy who has been a fixture of the ranch since Season 1, rushes in to save Carter. He succeeds, but the horse's thrashing hooves trample him to death.

I was the first in my family to go to college, which I did by working two jobs and joining the Army ROTC. In total, I served 30 years in uniform. **Life hasn’t always been easy, but my mantra has consistently been “ _service over self_.”**

Later on I joined the State Department and then served as a strategic advisor to the United States Army Cyber Command. **I don’t believe in partisan mudslinging — I have the best leadership and professional experience to deliver Pinellas and our great nation back to peace and prosperity.**

Now, my husband, daughter, and I have lived in the Tampa Bay area for more than 20 years. We watched neighbors struggle with skyrocketing costs of housing, healthcare, insurance, food, fuel, and groceries. We saw hurricanes destroy our homes. Our national security and coastal economy are in chaos while politicians drive hate among our neighbors and distrust among allies. **It’s time for change.**

I served 30 years in uniform, and now I’m running for Congress to fire Anna Paulina Luna. = | = My family didn’t have much money growing up. I was the oldest of three, and I saw my dad fight to keep his small business going and, at our hardest times, my mom counted out food stamps at the grocery store. Life hasn’t always been easy, but my mantra has consistently been “ service over self.” Later on I joined the State Department and then served as a strategic advisor to the United States Army Cyber Command. I don’t believe in partisan mudslinging — I have the best leadership and professional experience to deliver Pinellas and our great nation back to peace and prosperity. Now, my husband, daughter, and I have lived in the Tampa Bay area for more than 20 years. **Ten weeks.** That's how much time we have to reach voters in CA-27 before Election Day – and before I ask for your **[$3 support,](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137919208/642370193/954579451?refcode=em-8.25.26-rs&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MDE1MyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5MDBkYWI1Ni1kMGEwLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlmMWQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=9uGNdvLj7aNfsvWIr1m0x29N7Sx5Bwk9AoHmYORCMoE=)** I want you to know why I'm in this fight. Running for Congress was never my plan. I'm not a career politician. I've spent decades in service to our communities. In 2009, President Obama chose me to lead NASA as Chief of Staff. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137919209/642370194/954579451?refcode=em-8.25.26-rs&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MDE1MyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5MDBkYWI1Ni1kMGEwLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlmMWQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=9uGNdvLj7aNfsvWIr1m0x29N7Sx5Bwk9AoHmYORCMoE=) I went on to lead a local aerospace company, creating over 700 jobs in the Antelope Valley. I co-founded an organization to end the wildfire crisis burning through California. Then I watched our Republican representative go to Washington and become a rubber stamp for the MAGA agenda – while working families in our district kept struggling. That's when I stepped up to run for Congress. We faced brutal political headwinds. We flipped this seat anyway – one of the only Democrats in the country to flip a GOP-held seat in 2024. Now I'm defending it for the first time – and with Prop 50 passed, thousands of new voters have been added to CA-27. I have to introduce myself to them, all while the national GOP is doing everything they can to stop us. **[If we’re going to put a check on this administration, we need to flip the House – and we can’t do that without winning districts like ours. disclaimer_text: Paid for by Becca Balint for Vermont**
body:
| [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137919684/642371465/-785282667?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM0MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxYmUyZDk2ZC1kMmEwLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlmMWQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=r0fJAYEhR9uNZInRgPt2HYuxqO0xLUU3BX2GsbhNKoM=)
