Peter, I gotta get right into it today and state the obvious here: **Why on earth are we picking a trade war with Canada?** Here in Vermont, our ties to Canada are deeply woven into our communities. We have family across the border. Friends across the border. Businesses and customers who depend on one another every single day. **And Vermonters are pissed about what’s happening. Frankly, a lot of us are deeply hurt by it too.** The Trump administration has taken one of our closest friendships in the world and turned it into a petty, chaotic trade fight that could make life more expensive for people here at home. [_**If you’re as fed up with this as I am, will you chip in $10, $25, or whatever you can today to help me keep fighting for Vermont in Congress?**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137919685/642371468/1802995202?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM0MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxYmUyZDk2ZC1kMmEwLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlmMWQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=r0fJAYEhR9uNZInRgPt2HYuxqO0xLUU3BX2GsbhNKoM=) **[CHIP IN TODAY!](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137919687/642371470/1802995202?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM0MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxYmUyZDk2ZC1kMmEwLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlmMWQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=r0fJAYEhR9uNZInRgPt2HYuxqO0xLUU3BX2GsbhNKoM=)** Seriously, look at where we are. We are slapping tariffs on **Canadian hockey sticks, for crying out loud** , dragging French-language protections into trade negotiations, and changing the terms of deals at the last minute. And guess who gets caught in the middle of all this nonsense? **Vermonters**. About a quarter of Vermont’s electricity comes from Hydro-Québec. In parts of our state, our energy ties to Canada run even deeper.
Then there’s housing. We are already desperately trying to build our way out of a housing crisis, and Vermont relies heavily on Canadian lumber and wood products. If Trump starts driving up the price of the materials we need to frame homes, suddenly it gets even MORE expensive to build the housing Vermonters desperately need. **And for what?** What exactly are Vermont families supposed to gain from making electricity, building materials, and everyday goods more expensive while torching a relationship with our closest neighbor? [_**If you’re ready to help me fight back against this reckless trade war and make damn sure Vermonters aren’t left paying the price for Trump’s chaos, will you chip in $5, $10, or whatever you can right now?**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137919689/642371471/1802995202?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM0MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxYmUyZDk2ZC1kMmEwLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlmMWQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=r0fJAYEhR9uNZInRgPt2HYuxqO0xLUU3BX2GsbhNKoM=) There are ways to use strategic tariffs to protect American workers and industries. But this administration’s whiplash approach is creating uncertainty, raising costs, and damaging relationships that go back generations. And Canada is going to respond. Of course they are. Who wouldn’t? That slapback could land especially hard here in Vermont because our communities and economies are so closely connected. **We should be strengthening those relationships. We should be lowering costs. We should be helping Vermonters build homes and businesses and lives they can afford.** I’m going to keep fighting like hell for that. And I’m going to keep saying how ridiculous this is until the madness ends — Becca

Peter, We’ve been focused on Wisconsin since the very beginning of the NDRC's work. For years, it was a poster child for how Republicans could manipulate maps to lock in power. I saw it firsthand when I lived there — and in 2011, I spent weeks sleeping on the cold, marble floor of the state capitol building in protest of then-Gov. Walker’s anti-democracy power grab. But over the past decade, we've broken down that GOP stronghold on the maps by electing pro-democracy leaders and judges who believe in fair maps. **Now, that progress is on the line in this midterm election — from the highly contested governor's race to state legislative races that hold the keys to majorities in both chambers.** Each party believes they have a path to win a trifecta — and thus control so much about voting and legislative maps in the years ahead. Republicans think they can take us backward. **We’re fighting back through our Democracy Defender program, which aims to win the most critical state-level elections in the fight for fair maps all across the country. For a lot of states, these elections could be the whole ballgame.** [**Tomorrow, we’re just 10 weeks from Election Day — donate now to help the NDRC reach our fundraising goal to ensure that we make this a monumental November for democracy.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137919670/642371452/1548394306?refcode=don_ndrc_tier1_email_DemDefender6_email_20260825-NDRC-Tier1-DemDefender6_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=don&utm_content=20260825-NDRC-Tier1-DemDefender6_&utm_campaign=DemDefender6&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjFhZTJkOTZkLWQyYTAtZjExMS05YjMzLTAwMjI0ODJhOWYxZCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=c01eu-GRInPEAiIE6ZofUudosK5nYWTHkBsnU_lC37k=) | _If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:_

body:
As of today, Election Day is just 10 weeks away.
# [](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20260825-6641-footer&t=1&akid=6641%2E420207%2E8Veh44)
Peter,
As of today, **Election Day is just 10 weeks away** , Peter.
**10 weeks** to knock on as many doors and make as many phone calls to voters as possible before ballots are cast.
**10 weeks** to ramp up our organizing, build our progressive movement, and get every vote cast.
**10 weeks** to make the case for Medicare For All, justice and dignity for our immigrant neighbors, and overturning _Citizens United_.
**10 weeks** to fight for an economy that works for everyone, not just the billionaires.
**10 weeks** to elect bold progressives like Abdul El-Sayed and Will Lawrence in Michigan, Tom Perriello in Virginia, and Peggy Flanagan in Minnesota so we can flip the House and Senate and hold this administration accountable.
**I’ll be fighting every day of those 10 weeks.**
Not only to win re-election here in Seattle, but to power the progressive candidates across the country. That means rallies, canvassing, phone calls, and not leaving a single stone unturned.
**Because it’s critical that _when_ Democrats take back power, it’s not just more of the same — that it’s a fight for bold, progressive policies which will actually make a difference for working people.**
And I’m doing it all without taking a _dime_ of corporate PAC money. This campaign is powered entirely by grassroots supporters like you.
[**So Peter, if you’re with me, will you pitch in $10 or whatever you can to help me keep fighting for our progressive priorities in these final 10 weeks before the election?**](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/53428?c0=pj-em-20260825-1.ZiOW-S&refcode=em20260825-6641&t=2&akid=6641%2E420207%2E8Veh44)
**[Contribute $10](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260825-1.0yFDUA&amount=3&refcode=em20260825-6641&t=21&akid=6641%2E420207%2E8Veh44)**
In solidarity,
Pramila Jayapal
**[Contribute](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/pj-email-footer?refcode=em20260825-6641-footer&t=22&refcode2=6641_420207_8Veh44&akid=6641%2E420207%2E8Veh44)**

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. | | Friend, My Republican opponent was on the radio recently and was asked a straightforward question by a caller about special education funding. The question focused on the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act, or IDEA. He was completely unfamiliar with this law — and did not even know if it was state or federal policy. He wrote it down and promised to look into it, but he read the acronym back as "IDF" and referenced "Israeli Defense Fund," which has nothing to do with education! This would be funny if it were not so scary. IDEA is vital because it guarantees a free, appropriate public education to over 7 million students with disabilities. In this moment, when the Trump administration is cutting education staff, restructuring the agency, and proposing to shift oversight away from the Department of Education, IDEA remains the core legal shield preventing a return to systemic exclusion and inadequate school support. Every parent, educator, and advocate should be terrified by this. I do not expect every candidate to know everything about education policy. But at the very least, you should be familiar with the key issues, and IDEA is key. **Especially at a time when this administration is eroding education services and funding for the students who need it most.** As a teacher, I champion legislation to make our classrooms safer and more equitable for all students. That includes fighting for federal education funding to reverse the decades of chronic disinvestment in public education. clean_body: | | Friend, My Republican opponent was on the radio recently and was asked a straightforward question by a caller about special education funding. The question focused on the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act, or IDEA. He was completely unfamiliar with this law — and did not even know if it was state or federal policy. He wrote it down and promised to look into it, but he read the acronym back as "IDF" and referenced "Israeli Defense Fund," which has nothing to do with education! This would be funny if it were not so scary. IDEA is vital because it guarantees a free, appropriate public education to over 7 million students with disabilities. In this moment, when the Trump administration is cutting education staff, restructuring the agency, and proposing to shift oversight away from the Department of Education, IDEA remains the core legal shield preventing a return to systemic exclusion and inadequate school support. Every parent, educator, and advocate should be terrified by this. I do not expect every candidate to know everything about education policy. But at the very least, you should be familiar with the key issues, and IDEA is key. Especially at a time when this administration is eroding education services and funding for the students who need it most. Now let me tell you why this mission means so much to me. My name is Eduardo Verastegui. Several years ago, I learned firsthand about the horrific reality of child trafficking. What I heard broke my heart. Children were being bought and sold.
Families were being torn apart.
Lives were being destroyed. **I couldn't forget it.** **I couldn't stay silent.** I kept asking myself one question: **"What if it were my child?"** That question changed my life. What started as a film project became a mission and a calling. That calling eventually led me to help produce the film _Sound of Freedom_. **Not for fame.**
**Not for awards.**
**But because I believed people needed to see the truth.** For years, many people said the film would never succeed. Doors closed.
Studios walked away.
People told us to give up. **But when innocent children are suffering, silence is not an option.** And while the film helped awaken millions of people to this crisis, awareness alone is not enough. That is why we created the **Sound of Freedom Foundation**. Our mission is simple: **To stop the sale of God's children.**

clean_body: Updates from our week in the field| | | | | Friend, | | Welcome to another Kean for Congress weekly update. We are excited to keep you in the loop with the latest happenings and highlights from across the district. There are only 70 days left until Election Day - now is the time to get involved and pitch in to make sure that Tom gets re-elected! Thank you for staying connected, and as always, please feel free to reach out with questions and click any of the volunteer links below if you would like to get more involved. | | | | | | | ✅ Tom Kean Delivers $2.4 million to Phillipsburg Park ✅ | | Last week, Tom presented a $2.4 million check to Phillipsburg for Delaware River Park revitalization. This funding will go directly to revamping the recreation fields and help preserve open space in the town. “I am pleased to deliver this federal funding to Phillipsburg. Residents should be able to enjoy their local parks, and this $2,400,000 will fund the revitalization of the recreation fields so that families can continue to gather, play, and enjoy safe, well‐maintained community spaces for years to come.” \- Congressman Tom Kean Jr. | | | | | | | Field Update | | | | | | | | | | | | It has been a packed August on the campaign trail since the last update! Tom joined community members and local leaders in Hunterdon County for a Protect the Vote Rally, where he spoke about the need for Governor Sherrill to give voters full transparency to ensure all New Jerseyans have confidence in the security and integrity of our elections. He was proud to be joined by NJGOP Chairwoman Christine Hanlon, RNC National Committeewoman Janice Fields, the LD-23 Legislators, County Chairman Gabe Plumer, and County Elected Officials. Tom also stopped by the Hunterdon County Fair, where he had the opportunity to meet with residents alongside county and local officials and enjoy one of NJ-07's favorite summer traditions. He wrapped up this past Saturday at Canal Day in Wharton, connecting with members of the community alongside Councilmembers Vince Binkoski and Ana Jones and Assemblywoman Aura Dunn. The summer rain showers have not stopped our field efforts! In the field, you might have recently seen some of our door knockers in Bedminster, Berkeley Heights, Bethlehem, Branchburg, Bridgewater, Clark, Fanwood, Green Brook, Hackettstown, Hopatcong, Long Hill, Mount Olive, New Providence, Phillipsburg, Raritan Township, Readington, Roxbury, Scotch Plains, Summit, Tewksbury, and Wharton. We continue to hold weekly Phone Banks around the District and have weekend door launches in all six counties. Want to join us? Use the SIGN UP TO VOLUNTEER button below and details will be provided. Want to get involved? Join us at some of our upcoming weekly events! | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | Spotlight of the Week | | This past week, we said goodbye to our NJGOP Morris County Field Director Jake Ponte who left to pursue a commission in the U.S. Marine Corps. Thank you so much for the hard work - good luck, Jake! | Friend, I'm reaching out with a personal request:

[Will you donate $10, split between the Voter Protection Project and me, to our work to flip the Senate and finally hold Trump to account?](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/126426?t=6&akid=28110%2E878179%2EF9n-R4) | [DONATE »](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/126426?t=7&akid=28110%2E878179%2EF9n-R4)
---
We have an opportunity this November to change the course of our country.

Control of the Senate comes down to a net gain of four seats. Republicans know it as well as we do, and they are not planning to hold their majority by virtue of their policies and arguments. _They are planning to outspend us._

Dark money donors. Handpicked self-funders. Super PACs behind every vulnerable Republican on the map. All to hold onto their Senate majority.

And we know what a Republican majority does with its oversight power, because we have watched it sit unused for two years. They will do nothing.

The president has personally taken in billions since taking office, and this Senate has not asked him or his cronies a single question about it under oath. He has gone after the machinery of our elections, and this Senate has called it overreach to object. A Senate that will not use its subpoena power is a Senate that has decided the president answers to no one.

We must flip four seats to take power, and there are eight places to get them — North Carolina, Ohio, Maine, Alaska, Iowa, Florida, Mississippi and Texas. Every one is winnable and not one is safe.

A year ago, most people looking at this map would have said we had a brutal path. That changed because candidates decided to run in states that were not supposed to be competitive.

[Our ability to hold Trump accountable depends on a Democratic Senate majority. So I am humbly asking you to please chip in $10 to the Voter Protection Project and me to help us win the seats we need to flip the Senate →](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/126426?t=8&akid=28110%2E878179%2EF9n-R4)

##### Here is why it matters this week. The piece below explains who actually pays a tariff. You will not get that explanation from the outlets that keep describing this as a fight between two governments, because saying it plainly means saying the president is lying to the people paying the bill. _**-- Cliff**_
* * *
There is something uniquely pathetic about the United States government, under Trump, declaring economic war on Canada. It's like watching an elderly demented apartment dweller attack the neighbor upstairs with a flamethrower because the building stairwell has become a little squeaky.
The assault is remarkable. The intelligence and logic behind it are non-existent. But here we are. Donald Trump has once again reached for his favorite economic instrument: the tariff. Canada has apparently failed to appreciate the majesty of the Trump negotiating team threats. So Old Man Orange has answered with a 50 percent tariff on Canadian goods and the prospect of even higher duties on automobiles, trucks, parts, and steel.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ca3e116d-9892-4772-b6e4-3ec2bdac3922?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Trump claims his economic warfare is in defense of American workers. Actually, it is yet another large tax imposed on American consumers and commerce.
The elementary fact, which continues to escape MAGA world and most republicans in Congress, is that a tariff is collected from the American importer. It is not an invoice mailed to Ottawa. When an American company imports a Canadian product subject to a 50 percent tariff, the American company pays the government. The company or business can then absorb the cost, reduce its margin, find another supplier or pass the increase on to customers. In other words, the administration's grand crusade against Canadian products has the feature of making American products more expensive.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/59b96f7f-b332-455b-8160-240bcce16e26?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
This becomes especially absurd in industries where the United States and Canada have spent decades constructing integrated supply chains. The automobile industry is the most obvious case. Parts and components cross the border repeatedly before a finished vehicle emerges. The arrangement exists because geography and economics occasionally manage to accomplish something that politicians cannot: they persuade people to cooperate.
Trump is now attacking that cooperation with a tariff sledge hammer. The dim-witted Trump theory is that if Canadian parts and product inputs become more expensive, American manufacturers will miraculously produce everything domestically, cheaply and immediately. This is the sort of economic reasoning of an imbecile.
Factories cannot be conjured into existence by presidential proclamation.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/59b96f7f-b332-455b-8160-240bcce16e26?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Supply chains cannot be rearranged by interviews on Fox News or Newsmax. Skilled workers do not materialize because the Trump White House has yet again discovered the word "tariff." Building new domestic capacity requires years of investment, enormous sums of money and incredible patience - a key commodity absent from all things Trump.
And then there is Canada. Canada is not a hostile dictatorship plotting America's downfall from some hidden hockey rink.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/59b96f7f-b332-455b-8160-240bcce16e26?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Canada is America's polite neighbor and one of its oldest allies. Americans and Canadians share a border, an enormous commercial relationship, military alliances, families, businesses and an almost comically dense network of ordinary human connections.
Yet Trump treats Canada as though its leaders are backwards provincial warlords who are threatening to invade, rape, and pillage Buffalo.
The political consequences are easy to predict. Canadians, like Americans, possess a certain affection for national dignity. When Trump threatens economic punishment, Canadian are not going to respond by bowing down and singing the Star-Spangled Banner. Instead, Canadians will conclude, yet again, that dependence on the American market is a strategic liability and the best response is to go elbows up.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/59b96f7f-b332-455b-8160-240bcce16e26?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
In other words, the great Trump tariff crusade will only encourage Canada to trade less with the United States...

This email is a bit on the longer side, so](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137921368/642377260/1974481312?amounts=5,10,15,25,50,100,250&amount=5&refcode=email_082526_bio-RS&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MjY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhMDBmMmQ2YS1kOWEwLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlmMWQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=klMoRIfauZYs9v6CsSz2VU612vzpl_eqQb_yN7_AO4g=) [_if you don’t have the time to read more, I’m going to ask if you could pitch in $5 to my reelection campaign._](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137921369/642377261/1974481312?amounts=5,10,15,25,50,100,250&amount=5&refcode=email_082526_bio-RS&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MjY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhMDBmMmQ2YS1kOWEwLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlmMWQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=klMoRIfauZYs9v6CsSz2VU612vzpl_eqQb_yN7_AO4g=) [But if you have a minute or two to spare, please keep going!](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137921370/642377262/1974481312?amounts=5,10,15,25,50,100,250&amount=5&refcode=email_082526_bio-RS&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MjY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhMDBmMmQ2YS1kOWEwLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlmMWQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=klMoRIfauZYs9v6CsSz2VU612vzpl_eqQb_yN7_AO4g=)** When I moved to Oregon in 1987, right off an Amtrak train from the East Coast to rainy Eugene, I was excited about a new place to explore and find new friends. As I settled in, I found much more — a place where I could truly be myself. I fell in love with the beauty of the state and the openness of the people — and found a community I could call home. After going back to school and graduating from the University of Oregon, working in politics was not on my radar. My journey eventually led me to nonprofit advocacy work at Oregon Food Bank and then Children First for Oregon — fighting hunger, supporting financial stability for more people, and strengthening state policies around childcare for working families and healthcare for kids. It was through that work — listening to Oregonians, working on issues our communities are facing, and helping create real solutions — that I realized I could make an even bigger difference through public service. That led me to nearly 15 years of service in the Oregon legislature. [**As Governor, my focus remains the same: listening to Oregonians, tackling our biggest challenges, and building a stronger, brighter future for all of us.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137921371/642377263/1974481312?amounts=5,10,15,25,50,100,250&amount=5&refcode=email_082526_bio-RS&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MjY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhMDBmMmQ2YS1kOWEwLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlmMWQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=klMoRIfauZYs9v6CsSz2VU612vzpl_eqQb_yN7_AO4g=) It’s my honor to not just work for you, _but with you_. With your support and partnership, I’ve worked to lower costs, address our housing crisis, strengthen schools, expand mental health care, and defend Oregon from Trump’s dangerous agenda. But the work is far from over, especially with all the challenges that President Trump and a Republican-led Congress have presented us. After going back to school and graduating from the University of Oregon, working in politics was not on my radar. Peter, The Supreme Court just released an emergency order that allows the Trump administration to move forward with its attempt to impose new restrictions on mail-in voting before November’s midterm elections. In essence, the guys who did January 6th are looking to re-write the rules of an election that every poll shows them losing―and the Supreme Court gave the administration its blessing! **[We the People can still fight, win, and take back our power. But we need to force Congress to stand with us, and not the wealthy extremists warping our system every day. Tell Congress: I demand a plan to give power back to the people!](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm3_5hbu1DV_K1a9EsXVVRCLGGsmGPePxwvjeqbCtRCFM_QHd0N8jgjrkxipuT1vhbhV2qpZdpNTLENG9-LH9sGkTGviJtbYeziHa9Ly0fs0pqpQ9-_6jXSJ46Ymqoxo71H2XR0UD88ffI7aZNk8eFOpSilAgiUjOuuM_LPcJw-yg1wtNP-mNemF7VldT4vMDcrVo3OlUBJKcXUOZKFfuDvGMIOBWW-a_97WL82mLAK81pw/4th/ai1KL220RJuONG9Sy8vHaA/h0/h001.wMzMpVJcAQRs1yVRGhvyKadhezcvk1M6RsP8cNq_1uU)** **Once again, the Supreme Court’s right-wing majority is using its extraordinary power to help Donald Trump** expand his authority, this time over the basic rules governing how Americans cast their votes. Just weeks before voting begins in the midterm elections, the Court has opened the door for the Trump administration to upend longstanding election procedures and make it harder for Americans to vote by mail — a method of voting President Trump has repeatedly attacked as fraudulent even as he has continued to use it himself, including twice this year. And it did so through an emergency order, **without deciding whether the President’s actions are even legal.** **This is bigger than one case or one election.** Over and over again, this Court has weakened voting rights, expanded presidential power and allowed an increasingly unchecked executive branch to override protections Americans have long counted on. **The message is becoming unmistakable: when Donald Trump reaches for more power, this Supreme Court is too often willing to hand it to him.** **A healthy democracy depends on voters choosing their leaders, not politicians rewriting the rules to choose their voters.** Americans should be able to trust the Supreme Court to protect that principle. Instead, millions of people are being forced to wonder whether their ability to cast a ballot will depend on the political agenda of six unelected, lifetime-appointed justices. **That is why Supreme Court reform cannot be treated as an abstract debate or something we can put off until another day.** We need a Court that is accountable, ethical and worthy of the public’s trust. One that protects our democracy and our fundamental freedoms rather than helping the powerful accumulate even more power. **[Congress has the authority and the responsibility to act. Demand a plan from Congress to restore our democracy!](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm3_5hbu1DV_K1a9EsXVVRCLGGsmGPePxwvjeqbCtRCFM_QHd0N8jgjrkxipuT1vhbhXGaOY24PLpMQfdH1ZeL4T8UIOHrITjt5YzCGJtTus9MnUZX8VdKyYJqNatQHCiGqb4yNf3i49LRXEkqs7QVG5q0mO7G03qI9Ur9UUx98MpyedlnJyyZKZTYp3ccA0m7qJ21fBaZc6PrPQmwjjnvOKJLJkbnicYls3mOFS3vm2BTQ/4th/ai1KL220RJuONG9Sy8vHaA/h1/h001.CyzK7eMqgVxMYVkJ_xbyKnwj5bNkYTeGVCEzjBKxIfg)** Thank you, Stasha Rhodes

clean_body: | | Peter, The Supreme Court just released an emergency order that allows the Trump administration to move forward with its attempt to impose new restrictions on mail-in voting before November’s midterm elections. In essence, the guys who did January 6th are looking to re-write the rules of an election that every poll shows them losing―and the Supreme Court gave the administration its blessing! Once again, the Supreme Court’s right-wing majority is using its extraordinary power to help Donald Trump expand his authority, this time over the basic rules governing how Americans cast their votes. Just weeks before voting begins in the midterm elections, the Court has opened the door for the Trump administration to upend longstanding election procedures and make it harder for Americans to vote by mail — a method of voting President Trump has repeatedly attacked as fraudulent even as he has continued to use it himself, including twice this year. And it did so through an emergency order, without deciding whether the President’s actions are even legal. This is bigger than one case or one election. Over and over again, this Court has weakened voting rights, expanded presidential power and allowed an increasingly unchecked executive branch to override protections Americans have long counted on. The message is becoming unmistakable: when Donald Trump reaches for more power, this Supreme Court is too often willing to hand it to him. A healthy democracy depends on voters choosing their leaders, not politicians rewriting the rules to choose their voters. Americans should be able to trust the Supreme Court to protect that principle. Instead, millions of people are being forced to wonder whether their ability to cast a ballot will depend on the political agenda of six unelected, lifetime-appointed justices. That is why Supreme Court reform cannot be treated as an abstract debate or something we can put off until another day. We need a Court that is accountable, ethical and worthy of the public’s trust. One that protects our democracy and our fundamental freedoms rather than helping the powerful accumulate even more power. Thank you, Stasha Rhodes United for Democracy Paid for by United for Democracy. | | Sent via . name: Elissa Slotkin
subject: What I asked Pete Hegseth
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY ELISSA SLOTKIN FOR MICHIGAN
body:
Uniformed military shouldn't be deployed to interfere in our elections. Period.
# [](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/188?t=1&akid=2495%2E135344%2EJwAwBq)

See this guy?
[](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/9?c0=ebs-em-26.79HKre&refcode=em260821&t=2&akid=2495%2E135344%2EJwAwBq)
That is Secretary of Defense, Pete Hegseth.
Earlier this year, he came before the Senate Armed Services Committee to answer questions about the war in Iran, the defense budget, and other matters.
Among other questions, I asked this one:
Will you deploy the uniformed military to the polls to collect voter rolls or machines in the upcoming election?
He wouldn't answer.
So last week I asked again, but this time to Secretary Hegseth and General Caine, the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs.
[](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/4405?t=3&akid=2495%2E135344%2EJwAwBq)
I asked them to confirm a simple statement: that the Department of Defense will not send Federal troops to the polls or seize election materials of any kind. The DOD spokesperson said they would respond.
Because the truth is, after losing the 2020 election, we all know what the president did: he tried to prevent the peaceful transfer of power to a new Administration. But what people don’t know is that President Trump also had his Administration draft an Executive Order during that same 2020 time period, directing the then-Secretary of Defense to use the uniformed military to seize ballots and voting machines—specifically in Michigan.
He has since told reporters that he regrets not signing that Executive Order.
There is no shortage of issues out there, but this one is fundamental: the uniformed military shouldn't be deployed to interfere in our elections. Period. It taints our democracy. It taints our military. And it would set both down a course that may be hard to ever come back from.
Thanks for listening. And for doing your part to watch this issue over the next 2 months.
Elissa Slotkin

East Lansing, MI 48826

name: Sarah McBride
subject: Proud to work with Chris
disclaimer_text: Paid for by McBride for Delaware
body:
Since he was elected in 2010, Chris Coons has been a tireless and effective voice on behalf of Delawareans.
# [](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1269?t=1&akid=3743%2E21716%2E28C1n8)
Team, it's no secret that this year has been difficult. In moments like these, MAGA Republicans are counting on apathy. They want all of us to tune out and let them pass their agenda with no opposition. We can't let them win.
There is a lot of work ahead of us to win back Congress in November, and we are experiencing a time of unprecedented fear and division. **But I believe our values are stronger than the forces that seek to divide us, and there are few leaders who remind us of this more than my friend, Senator Chris Coons.**
[](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=mcb-em-20260825-2.Ga-gdd&refcode=em20260825-3743&t=2&akid=3743%2E21716%2E28C1n8)
[**He's running for re-election to continue serving Delaware in Congress, and I'm asking for your help to protect his seat and his voice ahead of the Primary on September 15. Will you split a donation between our campaigns? >>**](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=mcb-em-20260825-2.Ga-gdd&refcode=em20260825-3743&t=3&akid=3743%2E21716%2E28C1n8)
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=mcb-em-20260825-2.Ga-gdd&amount=5&refcode=em20260825-3743&t=4&akid=3743%2E21716%2E28C1n8)**
**Since he was elected, Chris has been a tireless and effective voice on behalf of Delawareans.** He's secured hundreds of millions to support infrastructure in our state. He's consistently passed bipartisan legislation — signed into law by presidents of both parties — which improved access to housing, protected our children online and in their communities from harmful online content and gun violence, strengthened global conservation efforts, and funded critical healthcare research. In the Senate, he's led the conversation on small businesses, climate change, affordability, and other issues important to Delawareans.
In Congress, we've been proud to stand against the MAGA agenda and work together to continue delivering for our constituents, bringing down costs facing families, expanding access to health care and child care, and defending reproductive freedom.
But I know there's so much more we can do to make people's lives better. If we're going to flip Congress in this year's midterms so that we can hold this administration accountable and pass a budget that puts the needs of regular Delawareans over Trump and his billionaire allies, it has to start by protecting Chris's seat and his voice in the Senate.
Republicans would love nothing more than to flip Delaware red; in fact, one of the candidates running against Chris in the primary was not only recently a Republican, but was actually the Republican nominee against our colleague, Senator Lisa Blunt Rochester, in the last election. We can't let that happen.
[**Which is why today, I'm asking you to split a donation between my campaign and Chris's ahead of his primary to help us keep Delaware blue and win back Congress. Chip in $5 or wherever you can afford >>** ](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=mcb-em-20260825-2.Ga-gdd&refcode=em20260825-3743&amount=5&t=5&akid=3743%2E21716%2E28C1n8)
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=mcb-em-20260825-2.Ga-gdd&amount=5&refcode=em20260825-3743&t=24&akid=3743%2E21716%2E28C1n8)**
Let's do this,
Sarah McBride
